> **Generated — do not hand-edit this table.** Each row's source is
> `_registry/<CR###>.row.md` (one file per CR); rebuild with
> `scripts/registers/gen_registers.py gen cr`. See [How a CR works](#how-a-cr-works).

The register of **planned change** — new work, not fixes. A CR is anything that adds or
changes behaviour versus the current build: a feature, a refactor, a process change, a
content or infra change. (Fixing something already broken is a **Defect** —
see [`../defect/def_list.md`](../defect/def_list.md).)

Governance rationale: decision **D-058** in [`../initial_specs/11_decisions/decision_log.md`](../initial_specs/11_decisions/decision_log.md).

## How a CR works

- **This table is generated — never hand-edit it.** Each row's source is
  `_registry/CR###.row.md` (one file per CR = a disjoint write-path); rebuild with
  `python scripts/registers/gen_registers.py gen cr`. A shared monolithic table gets *swept*
  on the shared `main` checkout ([CR081](CR081_registers_are_architect_write_only/CR081_registers_are_architect_write_only.md));
  one-file-per-item removes the shared write entirely.
- **Auto-file, proceed.** Saiful's prompt IS the approval. When he asks for a change, the
  **Architect mints the next `CR###`** (one minter, no ID-collision race); its **domain
  owner** writes `_registry/CR###.row.md` + creates the folder + files the CR doc, then
  implements — no separate approval gate. A web CR's row is written by `coder.web`, a backend
  CR's by `coder.api`, etc. — the register is no longer an Architect chokepoint (it only mints
  the number, which is domain-agnostic).
- **ID:** `CR###`, zero-padded, sequential, never reused.
- **Folder:** every CR gets `docs/forward_planning/CR###_<snake_case_topic>/`. It holds at
  minimum `CR###_<topic>.md` (what / why / scope / acceptance). All design docs, notes, and
  sub-specs for that change live in its folder.
- **Regenerate + pathspec-commit:** after writing/editing a row file, run the generator and
  `git commit -m "…" -- <your row file> docs/forward_planning/cr_list.md`. Never bare /
  `-am` / `git add -A`.
- **Commit tag:** the fix/feat commit carries `(AT:R<N> CR###)` after the summary, e.g.
  `feat(journal): search across entries (AT:R42 CR007)`.
- **Exempt from needing a CR:** process commits — handover wraps (`chore(handover)`),
  TestFlight/build version bumps, and docs-only commits. These keep the plain `(AT:R<N>)` tag.

**Status:** one of exactly five tokens — `proposed` · `in_progress` · `done` · `dropped` ·
`standing` (an ongoing order with no completion date, e.g. CR060's content-quality
mandate) — and nothing else. Qualifiers go in the description column.

**Enforced** (DEF203) by `gen_registers.py verify` and
`backend/tests/unit/test_registers_no_drift.py`. The vocabulary deliberately differs from
the defect register's: a CR is planned work that can sit in progress, a defect is broken or
it is not. This line previously omitted `standing` and the register carried `started`,
`partial` and `in progress` alongside `in_progress`.

A race window that authorises an irreversible action is still a defect. **Third instance of one shape in three days** — CR070 reported `DONE` without checking a verdict existed, DEF086 reported `UNASSIGNED` without checking a `GATE:` was recorded, this reported `AWAITING_AUDIT`/`AUDIT_PASSED` without checking the evidence was committed; three different agents made the third mistake, which makes it protocol rather than discipline. **Fixes:** both loop prompts now open self-locating (*the directory you found this file in **is** `<AUDIT_ROOT>`*; ask for a path rather than guess a layout); `watcher.sh` gains **`-t <seconds>`** with exit codes `0` found / `2` bad usage / `3` timed out, omitting it preserving the old unbounded loop; the auditor's step 1 **branches on how it was started** (spawned-for-an-item goes straight to the audit and must not watch; a standing session passes `-t` unless a human can interrupt); the architect's spawn-payload rule now requires sending the loop prompt's **full path** — the one token it cannot infer; and a shared `undelivered()` helper in **both** scripts asks git whether each lane file is tracked and matches `HEAD`, rendering a new loud **`UNCOMMITTED`** state (Architect-actionable) instead of `AWAITING_AUDIT`/`AUDIT_PASSED` — the same shape as CR070's `UNGATED`. Both degrade silently outside a git repo. **Verified:** timeout exits 3 at 4.03 s measured; `UNCOMMITTED` → `AUDIT_PASSED` observed live across the auditor's own commit; CR050 as positive control (verdict *is* committed, still `AWAITING_FIXES`); no other lane moved (15 `DONE`, 10 `UNGATED` unchanged); board render 0.63 s over 39 lanes. Residual stated: the check verifies *committed*, not *pushed*. Closes DEF087. | done | [CR074_watcher_bootstrap_and_delivery/](CR074_watcher_bootstrap_and_delivery/) | AT:architect |
| CR075 | 2026-07-23 | **Download the Sharia universe once a day and hold it.** Saiful: *"Why don't we download and hold it for other users? We can do the download every day."* Today the universe lives only in **process memory** — each container builds its own copy on first use, re-fetched no more often than every 900 s — so network sits on the request path (the first halal trade after a restart pays for the fetch), every restart re-downloads, two workers can hold two different as-of dates, and **a source outage of any length means `UNAVAILABLE` ⇒ every halal-flagged trade blocked** ([DEF093](../defect/DEF093_disabled_flag_blocks_every_halal_trade/)'s blast radius triggered by a bad minute on a host we don't control). For a filter a user turned on for religious reasons, *"we couldn't reach a CSV, so you may not trade"* is a poor answer when yesterday's list was fine and the standard itself only changes at rebalance. **It also closes the freshness gap nothing else could:** the parent-index mirror publishes no as-of of its own, so SPUS's date is currently the only staleness signal and a frozen parent list would go unnoticed — a stored row carries **`fetched_at`**, stamped by us, which *is* the missing signal. And it makes the claim defensible: constraint 1 requires naming standard + source + as-of wherever a verdict shows, and holding the list makes that date a fact we recorded rather than a property of whatever we happened to fetch — if anyone asks which companies AMI treated as compliant on a given day, a row answers it. **Design:** a small `coder.api`-owned table (standard, source URL, file `as_of`, our `fetched_at`, compliant set, parent set — two lists of a few hundred tickers, size is a non-issue); refresh via a background task in the **existing** pattern (`main.py` already runs `_nightly_audit_trim()` and `_league_roll_tick()` as startup asyncio tasks — **no new dependency, no new mechanism**), with a tick that finds a fresh row doing nothing so restarts can't miss a boundary; read path resolves from the row, so no network, no `asyncio.to_thread`, no first-request stall, and the in-process cache becomes a read-through rather than the source of truth. **Unchanged:** no failover/union/intersection (one named primary standard, §3a — holding one standard's list is not blending two); `sharia_screen()` stays dormant (constraint 4); blocking on genuine staleness stays (constraint 3 — this only buys a longer runway before it fires); G3 unknown-permits unchanged. **Open for the build lane:** whether a *held* list should be servable longer than a *fetched* one (stated, not inherited); first-boot seeding with an empty table and an unreachable source is still correctly `UNAVAILABLE`; and a refresh failing three days running while the list is still in-window must be visible to **us** even though it's invisible to the user — degrade-loudly applied to the refresher, not the reader. `GATE: independent` recorded upfront — it changes what an observance filter enforces and how it fails, and it touches the schema. **Laned 2026-07-25 (AT:architect):** single lane `CR075` → `coder.api` (schema owner), `GATE: independent`; diagnosis re-verified against current `sharia_universe.py` (in-process `_cache`, 900 s refetch throttle, `default_halal_universe()` blocks on two 15 s httpx round-trips on the request path, zero persistence). Build: new table (append-only recommended, `down_revision = a1c2e3f40020`) + `_sharia_universe_refresh()` background task in `main.py`'s existing `_league_roll_tick` pattern + read-through-of-row read path with the `frozenset`/`resolve` three-state seam byte-unchanged (safety_floor/sim_engine/room_runner untouched). Held-window length + latest-vs-history left as stated build-lane decisions per the CR's open questions. NOT bundled with CR055/056 (both DONE) — schema/migration surface. **Built + audited COMPLETE r1 + integrated (2026-07-25):** new append-only `sharia_universe_snapshots` table + Alembic migration `b2d3e4f50021`; `_sharia_universe_refresh()` daily background task; read path is now a read-through of the stored row (no socket on any request). The `resolve`/`HalalUniverse`/`_build`/`get` three-state seam is byte-unchanged, so `safety_floor`/`sim_engine`/`room_runner` + the 4 read-path callers are untouched. Decisions: append-only history (read = latest by `fetched_at`); 30-day reader hold-window distinct from the 7-day `sharia_staleness_days` (now the source-lag signal). Track-U verdict zero BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR; Architect independently re-verified from the repo root (scope 8 files, seam byte-unchanged, full suite green modulo one pre-existing Alpha-Vantage env-flake in `test_news_context`, unrelated). Integrated `9a3cfe9` (rebased off a stale coder base, zero-conflict). **Stays `in_progress`:** live repro on a promoted Alpha (restart ⇒ no first-request socket; source outage ⇒ held list served with its held as-of) pairs with CR055/CR056's live repro on the next promote. **Live repro PASSED (2026-07-26, alpha-2026-07-26-1 / `b798f84`, `SHARIA_SCREEN_ENABLED=true`):** on container boot the `_sharia_universe_refresh()` task fetched from the real source and wrote one `sharia_universe_snapshots` row — standard `AAOIFI`, `as_of=2026-07-24`, `fetched_at` stamped (the freshness signal), **216 compliant / 503 parent** tickers. | CR077 | 2026-07-23 | **Prompt caching is already on, delivers 0% on Room prompts, and could not have helped much anyway.** Saiful: *"lots of our messages to the llm are static, especially for the agents. is there a way we can speed up the processing by pre-caching a major part of the prompt?"* The premise is right; the conclusion doesn't follow. **Measured on the live serving host** (`192.168.20.74:8000`, vLLM `0.23.1.dev0`, `ami-llm` = `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`): prefix caching is **already enabled** (`enable_prefix_caching="True"`, lifetime 17,151,568/50,924,616 = 33.7% of queried tokens) — nothing to turn on. But `ami-llm` is a **Mamba/attention hybrid**, so vLLM auto-resolves `block_size` up to **2,096 tokens** to align the Mamba and attention pages, and caching is whole-block only. **Measured cliff: a 2,095-token prompt repeated verbatim reuses 0 tokens; 2,096 reuses a full block** — and every reuse observed was a multiple of 2,096 (2096/4192/6288/14672). Every Room agent system prompt is **1,143–2,264 tokens** (the static base+overlay part only 635–1,387), so the Room gets **exactly zero** cache benefit today; the 33.7% comes from elsewhere. Known upstream issue, not our misconfiguration — vllm-project/vllm #40696. The twelve agents also share **no** common prefix: `build_agent_prompt()` puts `content/agents/<id>.md` at token 0, so they diverge on the first token. **And fixing it wouldn't matter: prefill is ~4% of a turn.** Decode measured at **33.0 tok/s** single-stream (200 tok in 6.07 s, 400 in 11.89 s — same rate); prefilling a whole 1,300-token prompt costs **0.29 s** against **~7.6 s** to generate a 250-token turn. Perfect caching of 100% of every prompt cuts a convene ~4%. **The real lever is concurrency.** Same host, `min_tokens` forced, streams salted against cache cross-talk: 1→33.0 tok/s, 2→57.1 (1.73×), 4→91.1 (**2.77×**), 8→150.5 (**4.57×**) aggregate; and the card is at `gpu_memory_utilization=0.5` with 3.49M tokens of KV cache — half unused. `room_runner.py:1375-1393` runs all twelve agents strictly sequentially. Exactly one phase could change: **ANALYSTS** (fundamentals/market/news/social, four independent domains) — ~4×6.1 s becomes ~8.8 s, **~15 s off a convene, ~4× what perfect caching could ever deliver**. RESEARCHERS (bear answers bull) and RISK (three debators) must stay sequential — the dependency is the point. **The catch, raised by this lane not discovered later:** every prompt carries `Transcript so far:` and *"build on the transcript — do not repeat what's already been said"* (`room_prompts.py:214,220`), so concurrent analysts go blind to each other and will repeat. That is a **Room-quality** call, decided by reading real output, not by reasoning — hence **Phase 1 is a blocking A/B on 5 tickers, and no code ships before it**; if quality drops the CR closes at a documented "no". Phase 2 parallelises ANALYSTS only, behind a `parallel: bool` on `_Phase` with deterministic `RoomEvent` ordering; Phase 3 raises `gpu_memory_utilization` (ops on the LLM host — this workstation has no SSH to it). **Explicitly refused:** restructuring prompts to build a ≥2,096-token shared prefix. It moves the per-agent persona to the *end*, colliding with the safety-floor ordering rule (`agent_prompts.py:64-65` — the floor is appended last *so it dominates*) and CR038's ~70% instruction-compliance finding. Room-quality risk of that size for 4% of wall clock is a bad trade; revisit only if upstream lands sub-block caching. **Silent-failure trap recorded** for whoever does: in `align` cache mode (ours), if the Mamba checkpoint lands in request-unique tokens vLLM discards the *entire* prefix match including perfectly-matched attention blocks, and the hit rate drops to zero with no signal — vllm-project/vllm #45238. CR040's degrade-loudly class arriving from inside the inference server; hence the second guard, **log the measured hit rate at startup** — nobody would currently notice if caching were off. First guard: a test asserting the phases marked parallel are exactly the phases whose agents don't read each other — someone later marking RISK parallel would silently delete the risk debate while every test passes and the UI still renders three contributions, which is DEF084's shape. Also flagged in passing: CLAUDE.md's runtime table still says the LLM is *"Gemma 4 31B"*; the host reports **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4**. Brief — architect/build team implements; this lane files and reviews.  **AMENDED same day — Saiful: *"concierge take 20K token"*, and that flips the answer for one surface.** The Concierge system prompt measures **15,731 tokens**, of which **14,558 is the lesson catalogue** — `_full_context_index()` rendering all **342** lessons (`concierge_prompts.py:317`, CR020 `full_context`), **byte-identical for every user** and changing only when a lesson is added. That is 7 whole cache blocks of exactly the static text Saiful described — and it caches **nothing**, because `build_concierge_messages()` (`:103-131`) puts it **behind** ~900 tokens of per-user text (mandate overlay, mandate one-liner, journal, unlocked agents). A prefix cache matches from token 0 and stops at the first difference, so one differing mandate field invalidates all 14,558 tokens behind it; the cacheable prefix is `base` alone at **892 tokens — under the 2,096 cliff, so zero**. **Measured A/B against the live cache, two users differing only in mandate:** current order → 2nd user gets **0 cached, 2,672 ms**; catalogue-first → 2nd user gets **14,672 cached, 344 ms**. **7.8×, 2.33 s saved per message**, for the cost of moving one block earlier in an f-string. **Not oversold:** within one conversation the system prompt is already identical turn-to-turn, so today's shape already caches from turn 2 (measured same-user: 2,674 → 389 → 391 ms). The reorder buys **the first message of every conversation for every user after the first** — the message users actually notice. **Second-order win, arguably bigger:** today each user needs a private 15.7K-token KV copy (~222 concurrent contexts fit in the 3.49M-token cache, evicting Room traffic when they don't); shared-prefix, all users draw on **one** copy and need ~1K each — ~15× less footprint. **Safe where the Room reorder is not:** the catalogue is *reference data*, not instructions, so moving it reorders no instruction relative to another; the Concierge has no safety floor (PM-only); and the rules referencing it (*"never invent a lesson… name ONLY the lessons in that agent's list above"*) stay last. Becomes **Phase 0**, ships independently, with a guard test asserting the prompt head is **byte-identical across two mandates differing in every field** for ≥2 blocks' worth — the property the speedup depends on, silently destroyed by anyone later personalising one line of the head. **Phase 0 dispatched** as lane `CR077-CONCIERGE` (coder.api, `GATE: spawned`) 2026-07-23 after the Architect independently re-measured the mechanism against `192.168.20.74:8000` on a prompt built from scratch: catalogue-last → **0** prefix-cache hit tokens of 29,892 queried, 5,218 ms; catalogue-first, same brand-new user → **29,344** hit tokens, **284 ms** (metrics delta on `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total`). Serving config reproduced exactly (`block_size="2096"`, `_block_size_resolved="True"`, `user_specified_block_size="False"`, `enable_prefix_caching="True"`, `mamba_cache_mode="align"`), and the structural cause confirmed in code — `base` at `concierge_prompts.py:84` is itself mandate-derived, so nothing precedes the catalogue that is shared between users. Phase 2 (Room ANALYSTS parallelisation) **dispatched** as lane `CR077-ROOM` (coder.room, `GATE: independent`) 2026-07-23 after Saiful settled the Room-quality question on evidence: `news_analyst` quoted the Reddit sentiment score (social's domain) **while speaking before social**, so the four analysts draw on one shared data block, not on each other — Architect confirmed structurally (`room_prompts.py:338`, agent-independent profile). Phase 1's A/B **demoted from blocking gate to verification the lane attaches**. Hard condition: strip/rescope the "build on the transcript" line for the concurrent analysts. RESEARCHERS/RISK/VERDICT stay sequential. Phase 3 (`gpu_memory_utilization` 0.5→) **handed to the LLM-host team, not a build-fleet lane** — Saiful: *"we have a team taking care of it. do not touch it"* (2026-07-23). **Phase 0 INTEGRATED 2026-07-27 (AT:R65) at `882b1c9`** — audited **COMPLETE r1** by an Architect-spawned auditor that reproduced the live measurement itself rather than accepting the hand-off: **14,672 hit tokens / 318 ms** on a second user's first message vs **0 / 2,684 ms** old ordering (14,672 = 7x2096, whole-block; the shared-host contamination caveat did not bite — `query_delta == prompt_tokens` exactly on every request). 1 MINOR, non-blocking (a static divider was added to the head, so "only order changed" is slightly imprecise; it changes no instruction/lesson/routing/safety text). Builder died on its $5 cap mid-lane but had committed incrementally (DEF083 mode, nothing lost), and its hand-off misread `GATE: spawned` as "no auditor required" — PROTOCOL.md 4a means an Architect-spawned auditor, which is why one ran. **Phase 2 (`CR077-ROOM`) is AT AUDIT** on rebased tip `aec620c` (rebased onto CR026's room_runner/room_prompts integration per CR026 FLAG 1; both features verified together, suite 1304). CR stays in_progress until Phase 2 lands. **Phase 2 (`CR077-ROOM`) INTEGRATED 2026-07-27 (AT:R65) at `ea16a9d`** — audited **COMPLETE r1, zero findings**, by an auditor that re-read both 3-way-merge-conflicted files in full rather than trusting the rebase disclosure, re-confirmed CR026's sector-cap wiring intact on this specific rebased tip via *fresh* mutation testing, and mutation-tested both of CR077's own headline claims (the DEF084-shape parallel-phase guard and the actual concurrency) against production code rather than the test file's self-contained proofs. Post-merge suite **1320 green** from repo root, exit 0, integrated together with DEF112. **Not proven on the integrated SHA:** the 3.12x/~17s-per-convene speedup was measured pre-rebase on `8af991a`; the auditor declined to re-measure and explicitly left it flagged rather than accept or close it — do not quote it as measured on `ea16a9d`. Phase 3 (`gpu_memory_utilization`) stays with the LLM-host team, not a build-fleet lane, so **CR077 closes at done from our side**. | done | [CR077_llm_prefill_caching_and_room_latency/](CR077_llm_prefill_caching_and_room_latency/) | AT:R59 |

| CR106 | 2026-07-28 | **Room result: a graphical Verdict Board + a collapsed transcript, with the user choosing the default.** Saiful, relaying user feedback: *"the long technical result from convene the room \[is not\] good, most users do not want to read too much, so a graphical/iconical response (with the option to look at the full details) might be easier."* **Measured, not a taste call:** `room_screen.dart` renders a completed run as ONE `SingleChildScrollView` of 12 stacked `MarkdownBody` blocks — `_LENGTH_GUIDE` (`room_prompts.py:65-78`) budgets 30–40 sentences ≈ **3,500–6,000 chars ≈ 4–7 phone screens** before the verdict card, `_scrollToBottom()` pins the user to the bottom of it, and there is **no summary, sectioning, collapse or truncation anywhere** (zero `ExpansionTile`/`AnimatedCrossFade` in `mobile/lib`). Two aggravations: the size/entry/stop/target rows render **only `if (isApprove)`** (`:957`), so a PASS is prose and nothing else; and the Journal replay of the same run is strictly worse (`journal_detail_screen.dart:272-308` — no markdown, no metric rows, no hex avatars). No CR/DEF covered this (checked CR001–105, DEF001–130); the original spec anticipated it (`convene_the_room.md:95-105`, the v1.0 "visual deck… console collapsible"), and this CR redirects that from animated theatre to readable summary. **Decided with Saiful:** both modes ship (*"I like the verdict board, but I also like the collapsed transcript… let's give the user the option"* → persisted preference, first run = BOARD); per-agent stance comes from a **backend structured envelope, not a client-side keyword heuristic** (CR038 — a mis-tinted hex is a confident lie about what an agent said, the DEF059 class); and **this round is spec + prototype only, no code**. **Design.** Hero = a hex-marked KPI tile, not a giant hexagon (`hex_clipper.dart:85` records a label clipping inside hex geometry at 1.15 text scale — usable width is 0.724 of the box), covering **five** states incl. the two the current UI mishandles: `NO_VERDICT` (today amber, i.e. reads as a rejection) and `done && verdict == null` (today one bare sentence — an outage must never be shaped like an outcome); REJECT moves amber→red per `colors_motion_rtl.md`. Consensus comb resolves the core tension — tinting agent hexes by stance **violates "family colour is sacred"** — by encoding **stance as ordinal band position and conviction as a hexagonal ring sweep, hue untouched**; opacity/saturation ramps are forbidden (`hexCyan` clears the 4.2:1 floor only above ~70% alpha, *and* `Opacity(0.35)` already means "hasn't spoken yet" at `room_screen.dart:323`), as is a continuous lean axis (asserts precision an LLM-sampled stance can't support). **The comb holds 11 hexes, not 12** — the PM is the hero tile, captioned `THE PM DECIDES — THIS IS NOT A VOTE`, which kills any "consensus %" reading structurally rather than with a disclaimer. Collapsed rows **extract, never summarise**: the first `**bold**` span verbatim (agents are already instructed to bold key metrics by `_PROSE_FORMAT`, so it's a quotation and cannot be wrong), the Trader's level triple via `_LEVEL_PATTERNS`, an amber mark on `content.contains('[AMI')`; first-sentence truncation is **rejected** — Bull/Bear prompts ask for "thesis + evidence + falsifier" and cutting at 32 chars strands the negation. **Three backend gaps gate the pixels:** **B1** `verdict.level_provenance` — `room_runner.py:859-862` MINTS a missing stop/target at `entry*0.94`/`entry*1.13` and discloses it only by appending a sentence to `reason`; clamping that sentence behind a WHY expander *while* promoting the same numbers into a to-scale ribbon with a computed ratio makes an existing DEF059-shaped problem worse, so **no provenance → no ribbon** (side effect: every defaulted verdict is pixel-identical at R:R exactly 2.2:1); **B2** per-agent `{stance, conviction, headline}` envelope on the PM's proven JSON precedent, quantised in the schema, `null` surviving to the pixel (missing → gutter, never `neutral`); **B3** `opinions_not_included` + the `agent_withheld` SSE event, both emitted server-side and silently dropped client-side today. **B2 must land AFTER DEF125** (flat `max_tokens=400` truncates the RM mid-sentence in 66.1% of convenes — an envelope adds tokens), and rebase behind CR098/CR104/CR105, which all edit `room_prompts.py`/`_format_profile`. **Delivered this round:** the spec; a self-contained clickable prototype (`prototype/room_board.html`, 8 scenarios × 2 modes × dark/light × LTR/RTL × 1.0/1.15 text scale, fonts inlined as subsetted base64 woff2 because an Artifact's CSP blocks font CDNs and a silent fallback would mean reviewing the wrong typeface); and `docs/initial_specs/05_design/data_viz_and_meters.md` — the **missing data-viz chapter**, since the design-system mount's entire chart guidance is one line ("blue primary, green positive, red negative") and every chart shipped so far made local decisions. Prototype verification caught two real bugs that would otherwise have shipped: RTL bidi rendered `2.8 : 1` as **`1 : 2.8`** (a wrong number, not a layout nit — hence the LTR-locked ribbon + isolated numeric runs), and using the AA-safe accent *text* tones as *fills* turned the light-mode comb muddy (fills keep their tone, only ink darkens — now two tokens per accent). **Five defects spotted, flagged to the Architect to mint, not filed here:** `NO_VERDICT` renders as a rejection + leaks the raw enum untranslated; `RoomVerdict.fromJson` coerces unknown actions to `PASS`; `ShareService.shareVerdict` takes `isApprove`/`isPass` booleans so REJECT and NO_VERDICT produce identical share cards (and a board gets shared far more than prose); `opinions_not_included`/`agent_withheld` dropped; Journal replay worse than the Room. **SCOPE EXTENDED 2026-07-28 — the Decision Journal replay too.** Saiful: *"we need to implement this also in the journal when we display room results."* That surface is the worse of the two: `journal_detail_screen.dart:272-308` re-renders each contribution as a bare `Text(content)` with **no markdown parsing** (so `_PROSE_FORMAT`'s `**bold**` metrics reach users as literal asterisks), no metric rows and no hex avatars. **One widget, two mappers — not two renderers:** rebuilding the board separately for Room and Journal is DEF098's named class (*two independent renderers of the same data, neither a superset*), which is exactly how the Journal fell behind; extract `RoomBoard`/`RoomTranscriptRows` against a shared view-model and give each screen a mapper. **The Journal payload is a SNAPSHOT, not a `RoomRun`** (`build_journal_entry_for_run`): it carries the full verdict (incl. `opinions_not_included`), transcript and `model_tier`, but **never `duration_ms` or `credit_cost`** — so the strip reads `{TIER} TIER · MANDATE v{n}` there — and `live_data_notice`/`agent_withheld` are stream-only and absent. **Vintage degradation is the design point:** an entry written before a field existed will never have it, and re-fetching `GET /v1/room/{reference_id}` does NOT fix that (`RoomRunRow.verdict` is the same JSONB written in the same moment), so the board degrades **per entry** — no `level_provenance` → metric list, no ribbon, no ratio; no stances → the comb states *"stances were not recorded for this run"* rather than three empty bands; **never backfilled**, since an inferred provenance is a guess about a past decision wearing the authority of a record. Mode B degrades to nothing at all (it needs only `content`), which is why it ships first on that surface. **A journal entry is a record, not a setup:** prototyping caught the board offering `OPEN TRADE TICKET` against a June entry's $118.20 — a one-tap trade at a stale price; the Journal gets `SEE CHART` + `RE-RUN WITH CURRENT MANDATE` (what `screen_inventory.md:120` already specifies) and a `LEVELS AS OF {date} — A RECORD, NOT A CURRENT SETUP` caption. Prototype now carries 8 scenarios across both surfaces incl. a pre-CR106 journal entry showing the degradation live. **AGENT IDENTITY IN THE COMB, 2026-07-28.** Saiful: *"we will need to be able to identify the agents in the voices… since the groups share the icon colours."* Correct, and unfixable by colour: family colour is shared **by design**, so 3 cyan analysts / 2 purple researchers / 3 amber debators are mutually indistinguishable — and BULL vs BEAR, the pair a reader most wants to separate, are the same purple. **Three options built and compared at real size in the prototype (rail control *Hex identity*, kept so the call stays auditable): letters win.** Icons rejected — at 14pt only arrows/chevrons/equals/zigzag survive, the ledger/document/bubble/shield/merge glyphs are mush, and all eleven would make the reader learn a legend for something that already has a name; colour-only rejected because it IS the reported problem. Labels come from a new `combLabel` on `Agent`, capped at 4 chars (`FUND MKT NEWS SOC BULL BEAR RES TRD AGG CON NEU`) — only `RES-M→RES` and `TRADE→TRD` differ from the shipped `abbreviation`, i.e. a truncation, not a second naming scheme; 4-char at 7.5pt tightened, 2–3-char at 9pt, both scaling with text scale, band wraps rather than clips. **Conviction moves from the hexagonal ring to a 22×3pt underline bar** — the ring cost ~9pt of diameter, exactly the room a legible label needs, and given "how strongly" vs "who", **who wins**; length is a weaker magnitude channel than arc but still a magnitude channel, and unknown conviction still renders no bar at all. **Ink is slate900, never white** — measured `Colors.white` on `hexAmber` = **1.8:1** and on `hexGreen` = **2.1:1**, below even the 3:1 large-text floor; dark ink clears 7:1 on all six family fills and serves both themes since fills keep their tone. **Two further shipped defects found while sizing this** (now 7 flagged, not 5): `HexAvatar` sets its label in white on the family fill (live contrast failure on every Risk debator and the Trader, Floor honeycomb + Room transcript), and sizes it at `size*0.16` — 15.4pt on the 96pt Floor hexes it was tuned for but **4.5pt on the 28pt Room-transcript avatar**, i.e. a decorative smudge where a label was intended. Generalised into `data_viz_and_meters.md` §4.4 as a system rule (colour identifies a family, never a member). **SURFACE SHAPE CORRECTED 2026-07-28.** Saiful: *"the groups does not use hex-like design. look at the current journal design. It uses rounded edges rects."* The first prototype pass hex-cut its panels per the design-system mount, which specs `--clip-angle-panel` for cards/modals — but **nothing in `mobile/lib` implements that**: every content surface ships as a rounded rect (`AmiRadii.card` 8, `AmiRadii.sheet` 12 for `_VerdictCard`, same in `AccentCard` and every `journal_detail_screen.dart` block), hex clipping is reserved for **marks and controls** (avatars, chips, toasts, bottom nav, and `ticker_chart.dart:185`'s period toggle at `cornerCut: 8`), and Room CTAs carry no `shape:` override at all so they are Material-3 stadiums. **The app wins over the mount** — the feature lives inside those screens — and it is the better rule anyway: cutting the corners off every card spends the hexagon on chrome and leaves nothing to distinguish the marks that should carry it. Applied throughout; **hexagonal geometry now survives on exactly three things — the agent marks, the hero's outcome mark, and the BOARD|TRANSCRIPT toggle**. Recorded as a system rule in `data_viz_and_meters.md` §4.0, with a flag that `ami_hex_in_flutter.md` should carry the DS-vs-app divergence where the port is documented. **AGENT SELECTION FROM THE BOARD, 2026-07-28.** Saiful asked whether selecting an agent on the Board should switch to Transcript and open that agent's detailed entry. **Half of it — the destination is right, the trigger is not.** A 26pt mark is a casual target; tearing down the whole surface loses the board's scroll position and forces a hunt for the toggle to return; comparison is the *normal* case ("why is BEAR against?" is almost always followed by "what did CON say?" — four round trips under a mode switch); and a content tap must never rewrite a stored view preference. **Resolved: tap → a bottom sheet** carrying the agent's name/phase, `STANCE`/`CONVICTION` chips when known, the full contribution as parsed markdown and the AMI geometry annotation if present, with the board intact behind it — **and the sheet carries the asked-for destination as an explicit action**, `READ THE FULL DEBATE →`, which switches to Transcript, expands that row, scrolls it into view and briefly tints it. The mode switch then happens when the user asks for it, not as a side effect of curiosity. New trap **T-MODESIDE**: only the segmented toggle may call `setMode`; the jump changes mode for the screen only, or one curious tap silently rewrites what every future Room opens as. Withheld/empty agents get **no** jump action (a trip to a row reading `NOT HEARD` is a wasted one); the sheet hosts the same expanded-row widget the transcript uses, so there is still no third renderer (T-TWICE); transcript rows continue to expand in place, so the sheet exists only where the full text has nowhere to go. | CR108 | 2026-07-28 | **Lessons track hexes: wrap the label to two lines (do NOT enlarge the hex).** Saiful: *"maybe we can make the hex bigger and allow two rows. the main size issue is likely in the lessons."* Second half right, first half unnecessary — **measured**: the track hex is already ~143pt wide (`0.40` of available width, the largest hexagon in the app after `agent_unlocked_screen`), and the constraint is *where the label sits*, not hex size. `track_hex_button.dart:43` places it at `y=0.224` — above centre, above the progress doughnut — where a flat-top hexagon is only **0.724** of its box (103.5pt of 143pt), and it is locked to `maxLines: 1, softWrap: false` inside a `FittedBox(scaleDown)` at an 8px base, so a long label does not wrap, it **shrinks**. `ISLAMIC FINANCE` = 15 chars × 0.825em × 8px = 99pt in a 103.5pt box (the 4.7pt of headroom `hex_clipper.dart:85` already records); at 1.15 text scale it needs 113.9pt so FittedBox drops it to **8.4px** — below its own 8px base, and the only label in the set that gets *smaller* when the user asks for bigger text. **Fix:** `maxLines: 2`, `softWrap: true`, cap 8px→10px, and size against the **top line's** width (a two-line block centred on y=0.224 puts line 1 at ≈y=0.176 → 0.676 of the box = 96.7pt, not 0.724) — with the two-line fraction derived as a companion constant beside `flatTopHexWidthFractionAtLabel` so a future y-position change moves both. Only **3 of 13** labels wrap (`NEWS & MACRO`, `ASSET CLASSES`, `ISLAMIC FINANCE`); the other ten stay one line and take the higher cap. **Result: every label 8.0→10.0px at 1.0× (+25%), smallest at 1.15× goes 8.4→10.5px, and nothing shrinks below its base any more.** **Explicitly NOT enlarging the hexagon** — `0.40` is guarded by `honeycomb_layout_test`, and that guard exists because it was once set to `0.80`, rendering every hex at double size and overflowing the column 2×. **Also not in scope:** the CR106 consensus comb (bigger cells + wrapping there is only needed to carry *icons*, which needs ≥44pt cells → 6 per row → the FOR band wraps → ~+100pt of board height; letters at 26pt are already legible per the CR106 prototype and CR107's rule puts the comb below the icon threshold), and icons in the track hex (CR107 §3 keeps lesson *tracks* out of the agent icon program — different entity). Acceptance flags that `honeycombTrackLabel` is hardcoded English with no ARB coverage — the same gap CR107 §1 raises for agent names — so wrapping behaviour for longer AR/MS translations is untested by definition. **RULED (Saiful, 2026-07-29): APPROVED to build, bundled with DEF154 as one mobile-legibility pass.** Not because they share code — CR108 is `track_hex_button.dart` and DEF154 is `hex_avatar.dart`, different widgets on different entities — but because they share a *verification cost*: both change type rendering across many surfaces, both need Saiful's eye on a physical device, and shipping them separately means two builds, two device checks and two TestFlight round-trips for what is one judgement call about whether the lessons screens read properly. **DEF142** is queued on `HexAvatar` too and should be folded into the same pass rather than becoming a third trip. The sequencing consequence is recorded on CR107: that CR is HELD until this pass lands, because DEF154's font floor is the control for whether its icon program is needed at all. Spec: [CR108_lessons_track_label_two_lines/](CR108_lessons_track_label_two_lines/). **ROUND 1 BUILT AND REJECTED — pre-audit, by the Architect (2026-07-29, AT:R65). Nothing reached `main`.** Built on `lane/DEF142.coder.mobile` @ `846e92cd` alongside DEF142; the lane reported 306 green and 27/27 on its own new `track_hex_button_test.dart`. **It does not work, and the test proving it works cannot fail.** Three facts, each measured against the real render tree at the lane's own 143.2×124 fixture. **(1) The wrap never happens.** `FittedBox` lays its child out with *unbounded* constraints, so `softWrap`/`maxLines: 2` can never break a line — `RenderParagraph.size.height` reads **14.0, one line, for all 13 labels**. The new `flatTopHexWidthFractionAtTwoLineLabel` constant is applied to the `SizedBox` *around* the `FittedBox`, never to the text that is supposed to wrap, so the two-line branch is dead code at every geometry rather than just this one. **(2) The labels are therefore still being shrunk — the exact behaviour this CR exists to remove — and five are now SMALLER than before the change**, including `ISLAMIC FINANCE`, the one label the CR is named for: 5.64px → 5.47px, with `ASSET CLASSES`, `FUNDAMENTALS`, `NEWS & MACRO` and `FOUNDATIONS` also regressing. (Relative measurement under `flutter_test`'s fixed-width font — the before/after comparison is valid because both sides share it; the absolute pixel values are **not** a device claim.) The mechanism is font-independent: raising the base 8→10px makes the text 25% wider and the box narrows 103.7→96.8, while the wrap that was meant to absorb that never engages. The four short labels that never scaled (`RISK`, `EDGE`, `QUANT`, `ETHICS`) do get the full raise to 10px — so the change helps the labels that were never the problem and hurts the five that were. **(3) The guard is vacuous.** `paragraph.getTransformTo(null).getMaxScaleOnAxis()` returns **1.000 for every label** — it does not observe `RenderFittedBox`'s paint-time scale — while the painted rect proves real scaling is happening (`ISLAMIC FINANCE`: paragraph 177.0px, painted 96.8px). So `_renderedLabelFontSize` computes a constant and all 26 size assertions reduce to `expect(10.0, greaterThanOrEqualTo(10.0))`. **Proven by mutation: setting `needsTwoLines = false` — deleting the entire feature — leaves all 27 tests green.** The lane's own comment reasons correctly about why reading `Text.style.fontSize` would be wrong, then substitutes a second metric that is also blind and never validates it against a known-scaled case; `tester.getRect(finder).width / RenderParagraph.size.width` is the metric that works, because `localToGlobal` applies the paint transform. Also measured: **9 of 13** labels exceed the one-line box at this fixture, not the "exactly 3" the hand-off claimed — nothing depends on the count, since none of the nine actually wrap, but it shows the claim was reasoned from the three labels this row discusses rather than measured across the set. **Re-laned as round 2, Part B only** (`orchestration/dispatch/lanes/DEF142.assign.md`), with the bounded-text fix, the corrected metric, a `paraH` two-line assertion, an explicit decision for the unbreakable-word case (`FUNDAMENTALS`, 12 characters, cannot wrap at any width and must fall back to scaling), and a **mandatory** mutation showing the new assertions RED. **DEF142's Part A is accepted and untouched by this** — its census floor and contrast extension are sound and its own mutation goes RED. **CR107 stays HELD**: it was waiting on this pass as its control, and the control is not yet valid. **ROUND 2 BUILT (coder.mobile, AT:R65, 2026-07-30) — the mechanism, not just the metric, was wrong; both are fixed now.** Round 1 wrapped the `Text` in a `FittedBox`, which always lays its child out with *unbounded* constraints, so `softWrap`/`maxLines: 2` never had a width to break against. The fix moves the bound: the two-line branch now gives the `Text` its width from a plain `SizedBox` (no `FittedBox` at all), so real line breaks happen; `FittedBox` is kept only for the single-line branch, which is the half of the mechanism that already worked pre-CR108. Whether a candidate wraps is now *confirmed*, not assumed — `TextPainter(maxLines: 2, maxWidth: twoLineBox).computeLineMetrics()` must return >1 line with every line's width inside the box, or the label falls back to the single-line `FittedBox` scale-down path instead. **The unbreakable-word case, measured rather than assumed:** the round-2 assign named `FUNDAMENTALS` (12 characters, no space) as unable to wrap and required an explicit fallback decision for it — measured against the real render tree, that premise does not hold. Flutter's default line breaker splits an unbreakable "word" at the character level as a last resort when `maxLines` allows a further line (UAX#14 fallback), so `FUNDAMENTALS` wraps into e.g. `FUNDAMENT`/`ALS` and meets the floor at full size like every other label — it never reaches the fallback branch. That branch is still real and load-bearing; a synthetic 36-character single "word" (`SUPERCALIFRAGILISTICEXPIALIDOCIOUSXX`, no shipped label is this long) proves it triggers correctly (`geometricScale` 0.24, one line, not two). **The metric, replaced and validated before being trusted:** round 1's `paragraph.getTransformTo(null).getMaxScaleOnAxis()` does not observe `RenderFittedBox`'s paint-time scale and reads `1.000` unconditionally — reproduced directly in the new test file, not just asserted in prose. The replacement, `tester.getRect(finder).width / RenderParagraph.size.width` (goes through `localToGlobal`, which does apply the paint transform), is validated against a harness forced to a known 0.5× `FittedBox` scale before being used on the real widget. A `paraH` assertion (`RenderParagraph.size.height` two line-heights, using a same-harness single-line label as the reference rather than a bare `TextPainter` — the ambient `MaterialApp`/`Scaffold` `DefaultTextStyle` merges in a `height` the bare painter never sees) makes a silently-unwrapped label a visible failure, which round 1's assertions could not produce. **Mutation, mandatory this round:** reverting to round 1's `FittedBox`-wraps-`Text` structure turns 21 of 31 assertions RED, including the new `paraH`, `geometricScale`, and metric-sanity checks — restoring the fix returns all 31 to green. **Re-measured against the `8bb00594` baseline** (the pre-CR108 8px single-line-only mechanism), all 13 labels, at both 1.0× and 1.15× text scale, using the corrected metric on both sides: every label is equal to or larger than its baseline, none regresses (`ISLAMIC FINANCE` 5.64→10.0 at 1.0×, 5.78→11.5 at 1.15×; `FUNDAMENTALS` 7.05→10.0 at 1.0×, 7.23→11.5 at 1.15×; the other 11 similarly non-decreasing) — full table in the hand-off. Full mobile suite green (382, up from the pre-merge 306 — `main` gained other lanes' tests in the interim), `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos` exit 0, the same 5 pre-existing infos named in the assign. **Not independently verified against a physical device** — GATE is independent; this is coder.mobile's own measurement, pending audit.
