| CR109 | 2026-07-30 | **[HIGH PRIORITY — Saiful] The Game: a P&L competition in AMI Cash, separate from the training sim.** Saiful: *"This is a new game. Specifically designed for P&L of your AMI CASH. Measured only by the win/loss during the game period"* — weekly / monthly / quarterly / 6-month / annual — plus *"career points (for personal satisfactions)"*, a restart when *"you have lost too much"*, and *"when you re-start, the points you've lost will still hit your career points"*. **Depends on CR133 (bottom-nav restructure) and must be developed with it** — CR109 assumes the game has a home in the shell but deliberately does not say where; §13.1 records why sequencing them apart fails (the game ships with nowhere to live, or the nav ships with an empty tab). **Also depends on CR134 (design conformance review, AT:UI Designer): the game screens ship in CR134's corrected patterns, not the drafted ones** — hex geometry for controls (not rounded rects), colour by agent-family not literal-cyan CTAs, fill/dash provenance encoding (never opacity/saturation dimming), mirror surfaces stay colour-neutral (no amber scold), and ceremony motion is a bounded ≤600ms one-time draw-on rather than continuous animation. CR134 found zero hexagons across all 20 mocked screens and no design criterion anywhere in §19's ~60 acceptance items; its §3 criteria are folded in as new §19/§21 acceptance below, laning does not proceed on the drafted screens as-is. **Amendment A — no longer additive:** *"remove the current (boring!) reputation game"* — replaces `reputation_service.py` + `league_service.py` + `league_screen.dart` + badges + streaks, which scored process only (`lesson_passed: 5`, `room_verdict: 3`) and stated *"no P&L-linked event exists or ever will"*, so today a user can top the weekly league without their portfolio ever making money. Folds in CR063's in-app rules surface; **CR063 and CR093 close as stale**. Data left untouched, no migration — *"We are in Alpha. No real users yet"*. **Amendment B — Saiful rejected round 1 as a game: *"we only have a design, not a game design."*** Diagnosis: **five concurrent windows over one NAV curve is not five games, it is one game reported five times** — one set of decisions, five scores, no separate strategy or tension per cadence. **Amendment C — *"concentrate on making CR109 bullet proof… How do you propose all the game elements will fit? You need to have the full design."*** Navigation removed and reassigned to CR133 (it was scope creep into a change with its own blast radius); the organising model added; and the gaps a scoring spec leaves now filled. **THE SPINE — a three-layer model with a one-way rule.** Layer 1 **the Stake** (AMI Cash, positions, NAV — resets every entry); layer 2 **the Contest** (TWR, field, rank, placement `p` — collapses at close); layer 3 **the Record** (career points, titles, flair, cosmetics — never resets). **Value flows UP, never DOWN.** This is not a slogan: it *derives* the choices that otherwise look arbitrary — flat 10,000 capital for everyone (the Record can't buy Stake), cosmetic-only rewards (the Record can't buy Contest advantage), tokens refused (money is a fourth layer outside the game; paying in makes the Record convertible, paying out makes Stake purchasable), % TWR never absolute AMI Cash (else a bigger Stake buys rank and plan tier is pay-to-win), placement not raw return (raw return leaks *market conditions* into the Record, recording *when* you played not how well), and day-one competitiveness (a new player has a full Stake and an empty Record, and the Record never enters the Contest). The title multiplier is the one element that looks like a downward flow and isn't — it multiplies **within** layer 3, so scores compound with seniority while two players in a field always face identical conditions. **A run is an entry, not an account** — 10,000 AMI Cash fresh at entry, same at every cadence, own open/close/board; everyone starts dead equal on day one, the mid-period-join problem vanishes, every run has a natural ceremony boundary. Entry closes at the bell; **entry is free and always will be — an entry fee is *consideration*, one of the three legs of the gambling test**. **One live run per cadence** (answering *"can you enter multiple long term games?"* — no: the `+100`/`−40` curve makes parallel entries strictly +EV, so 12 rolling Annuals played maximally aggressive is a farm). **Full run/entry state machines** (`ANNOUNCED→ENTRY_OPEN→LOCKED→LIVE→SETTLING→CLOSED→ARCHIVED`, plus `ABANDONED` when a demand-gated field never fills, and `ENTERED→ACTIVE→FINISHED|FORFEIT|VOID`), scoring idempotent at close. **Trade rules were never specified and contained a live exploit:** `sim_engine.submit()` fills at the current quote whenever called, so outside US market hours a player trades against a stale last price *already knowing what happened after it* — harmless in training, a time machine in a scored contest. **Fills only during market hours; out-of-hours orders queue to the next open.** Explicitly NOT covered by the no-rules decision, because it is the difference between simulating a market and simulating one with hindsight. Also settled: long-only (`sim_engine` models no short), market orders, fractional allowed, cash earns nothing (interest would reward sitting out), no leverage ever, open positions marked not liquidated at close. **Thin fields — the most serious hole, from Saiful (*"on a new platform, we may find a month with a single player!"*):** `p=(n−rank)/(n−1)` is **undefined at n=1** and a coin flip at n=2; **a field of one pays the game's largest prize for beating nobody**; and rolling starts **break the very property that justifies placement** (§6.2 chose it because everyone in a field faced the same market), so merging cohorts across start dates — the obvious first idea — cannot work. Fixed by demand-gated rolling starts, **benchmark-relative career points below the placement threshold** (`alpha = TWR − benchmark`, preserving the exact market-cancellation property placement was chosen for, working at n=1, needing **no new infra** since `current_history()` serves SPY with a source flag and `portfolio_stats.beta()` ships), and titles requiring a real field. Degrades loudly: *"Field of 3. Scored against the S&P 500, not against the field."* **This is the DEFAULT path at alpha field sizes, not a fallback** — ships in phase 1 or phase 1 ships a divide-by-zero. **Rewards (Saiful: *"What do they get for being Champion?"*)** fall out of the one-way rule: **competition rewards are never purchasable and purchasable things are never competition rewards** (a trophy you can buy isn't a trophy, and it would give the Record a market price), and **no reward may improve future performance** (else the game compounds toward whoever won early). Tokens refused. Density scales inversely with cadence frequency — 52 weekly champions a year can't all get something permanent: weekly gets points only, monthly a badge, **quarterly a displayed title riding your handle on every board next quarter** (temporary but *worn*, the strongest cheap reward), half permanent flair + agent frame, annual a never-expiring title + agent skin + **a plaque in the Room** + Champions invitational. **Agent cosmetics are the best reward idea but there is no art** — `mobile/assets/` has zero portraits, agents render as icons + a resolved accent — so a skin means `accent + hex frame + material treatment`, which the design system already generates programmatically: zero art cost, on-brand. **What the other 25 get matters more than the champion prize** (one winner in 26 = twenty-five got nothing = churn): every close yields a progress marker where one is true. Free win: `BadgeRow.is_permanent_flair` exists from CR092 and `GET /v1/league/badges` ships live with **zero Flutter reading it**. **Edge cases specified:** field never fills, field of 1–2, halted/delisted mid-run, **anonymous→claimed mid-run (`merge_service.py` does NOT re-key `BadgeRow`/`StreakFreezeRow` today — a pre-existing gap that would strand a player's record at the exact moment they create an account; this CR must fix its own tables)**, account deleted mid-run, container restart mid-settlement, US-market-time boundaries. **NO ARENA RULES — Saiful's call, reaffirmed after argument:** the game path skips `check_mandate_compliance` entirely — no position/sector/drawdown cap, no cooldown, **and no halal / locale / long_only screen** (the halal screen is `if c.halal:` at `safety_floor.py:289`, inside that same function). **Accepted risk recorded the way D-060 was: a halal-only user trades unscreened on a scored path.** Obligations that aren't gates: the entry surface must **disclose** it (a screen that silently stops existing is the CR040 failure mode) and the training safety floor stays mandatory. **The split is load-bearing:** `sim_engine.py:607-640` already hard-rejects mandate breaches (so round 1's concentration risk was *overstated*), but `MandateRow` is keyed on `user_id` and Settings can edit it, so **on a shared account loosening your own mandate is a win-the-game move**; and `resolve_mandate` falls back to a **client-supplied** `mandate_override` while the mandate row is only created at claim, so an anonymous player supplies their own rules. **Ceremony:** entries-close countdown, the bell, one rank beat per US close (never per tick — that's a slot machine), the final stretch, a **settlement freeze** withholding results ~1h, the full-screen Close, the permanent record + share card, a dignified **Wind-Up** so a blowup is a chapter not a fail screen, and multi-category **Annual Awards** (more categories = more winners). Plus a **notification matrix** — and **push does not exist**, the only trace repo-wide being `note="TODO B1: fire APNs push notification here"` (`room.py:134`), so the anticipation layer is inert until its own CR. **Infra blocker, D-060's own third objection still literally true: no NAV/equity-curve/snapshot table exists in `models.py`.** `portfolio_nav_daily` must be append-only, user-scoped and **must NOT FK to `sim_portfolios`** — `reset_portfolio()` hard-deletes the portfolio and every `SimTradeRow`, so a FK cascades the game's history away; key on `user_id`+`run_id`. **Compliance is why this is not laned:** four documents forbid it — `roadmap.md:138`, **D-060** (`decision_log.md:302`), `daily_and_streaks.md`, `competition_rules.md` v1.0 §8 — and CR064 bound the zero-P&L rule as *a binding invariant, not a design note* because the store's "simulated gambling: No" answer depends on it. Mapped against the three-leg test: **consideration absent by design** (free entry), **prize absent by design** (cosmetic, non-purchasable), leaving **chance-vs-skill** as the live question — which the no-rules decision pushes toward chance at short cadences and cadence weighting pushes back on. Awarding credits on a P&L outcome is the step that needs the lawyer. **Phased as thin slices, because the monster is smaller than it looks:** at alpha field sizes the entire Contest layer is nearly inert — every field sits below the placement threshold, so runs score against the benchmark anyway, which makes **cohorts, demand gating, the placement curve, titles and the multiplier scale features rather than launch features** (building them first builds machinery that cannot run). Slice 1 (NAV table + tick + `twr.py` + the equity curve on the *training* portfolio) and slice 2 (game portfolios, entry, the game trade path, restart, the merge fix) carry **zero compliance surface**, so engineering starts while the legal work runs in parallel; slice 3 (scoring pass + benchmark scoring + career ledger + the Close) is the **first playable game**; slice 4 (the open board, placement, titles) turns on when fields clear n≥8. **The volume is not the risk — the coupling is:** CR109+CR133 can be *developed* together and *shipped* apart, with the game living behind the Floor card until CR133's destination exists. Implementation package ready for laning — schema DDL, API contracts, module boundaries, the fence against reusing the training submit path (**no `skip_compliance` flag** — extract shared mechanics and keep two public entry points, so the difference is structural per CR040), lane split and a 21-row test matrix: [implementation_plan.md](CR109_pnl_game_ami_cash/implementation_plan.md). **Playability reviewed** ([playability_review.md](CR109_pnl_game_ami_cash/playability_review.md)) against *"will this game be easy to start? will it be addictive? what brings back the player"* — verdict: coherent but **not yet playable**, and the worst flaw was self-inflicted. **Dead start (defect-grade, now fixed in §4):** entry-closes-at-the-bell plus fixed calendar starts meant a player arriving Tuesday could not enter until the following Monday — first experience of the headline feature was *"come back in six days."* Fixed by **rolling starts at every cadence** (weekly fields open every trading day, monthly weekly, Q/H/Y on the demand gate); everyone inside a field still starts the same day, so same-clock fairness is untouched. **Verified engagement risk: this CR deletes the app's only daily-return mechanic** — `streak()` lives in `reputation_service.py:271`, which Amendment A removes, and the game's heartbeat is *weekly*; recommended fix is to re-home a streak onto **runs finished / periods entered** rather than check-ins (a query over `game_entries`, not a subsystem). **The game is also the app's *unsupported* mode** — training has 12 agents and a safety floor, the game deliberately has neither yet is scored and permanent, so a beginner's first game action is "pick a stock" with no help and real consequences; gating first entry behind a training milestone is recommended but needs Saiful's call. Also flagged: ~5 days to first feedback with an empty day 0, and a first close that at alpha reads *"1st of 3, scored against the S&P"* — deflating, so §8.4's progress markers move from slice 8 to slice 3. Hooks ranked honestly, with the uncomfortable note that the strongest one (open positions / loss aversion) is the psychology the curriculum exists to warn about — which is why §10's *one beat per market close, never per tick* rule matters more than it looks. **DUELS BROUGHT BACK (Saiful: *"I really like the Dual….. how can we bring it back?"*) — as slice 3b, sequenced BEFORE the open board, because the review's central finding inverts their position:** the open board needs `n ≥ 8` to mean anything and every alpha field is below that, so the flagship competitive surface is inert exactly when the product most needs players to feel something — **a duel needs `n = 2`**, making it the only competitive format that works at launch, and it turns the first close from *"1st of 3, scored against the S&P"* into *"you beat VECTOR_11 by 1.4%."* Two constraints: **head-to-head scoring carved out of both existing paths** (never the placement curve, since at `n = 2` `p` is exactly 1.0 or 0.0 and the winner would take the largest award in the game; never the benchmark path either, since `n = 2` is intended here rather than a shortfall), and **auto-matched only at MVP** — anonymous-first onboarding makes alt accounts nearly free, so direct challenge-by-handle is a trivial collusion farm (make an alt, throw the duel, bank the win); auto-matching removes the ability to choose your victim, closing it structurally rather than by detection. **House desks (Saiful: *"we can run 'bot' players to make up the league, and we can have the bot players challenge the real players for a duel"*)** — the answer to what scoring alone cannot fix: §6.6 keeps the *numbers* honest in a thin field but cannot make a board feel alive or supply a duel opponent when no other human is online. They fill the board at every cadence, issue declinable rate-limited duel challenges, win duels sometimes (an opponent that always loses teaches nothing), and count toward career points. **Disclosure was chosen undisclosed, then REVERSED by Saiful on his own argument:** *"if we do not disclose that it's a bot, then if the copy happens (and it can happen off app) the user is copying what they thought is a person!"* — the decisive framing, sharper than the licensing objection that preceded it: the harm is that **the user's belief about the source is false** (they think they are copying a person who knows something, not a strategy that did well), and once a result leaves the app in a screenshot there is no disclosure surface left. So desks compete under **published strategy names** — Momentum Desk, Index Desk, Dividend Desk — never the word "bot", because a *desk* reads as a rival worth beating. Disclosure buys four things: copying becomes **education** (Saiful's *"I would copy the bots trading!"* is the feature working once the rule is published — studying a stated method, not chasing an anonymous winner, which is what `rejected_features_register.md` rejects); it removes the **advice exposure** of a hidden house account whose trades users follow from an entity not licensed to give investment advice; it **dissolves the title tell** Saiful spotted (*"it would be a bit of a give-away if they can be seen winning, but did not win title"* — an exclusion you can observe advertises what it conceals, but with disclosure "house desks are ranked but do not hold titles" is simply a rule); and it **lets them enter every cadence**, where the undisclosed variant would have had to stay out of Quarter/Half/Annual to avoid that tell — precisely the fields that are thinnest and stay thin longest. **Integrity line, separate from and harder than disclosure: a desk's P&L is never generated, sampled or tuned to look plausible.** Desks run real rule-based strategies against real prices through the same game trade path, because desk results feed real users' career points — a fabricated return would land in a real person's permanent Record, the DEF059 shape and exactly the silent-fallback failure CR040 exists to prevent. Roster includes a **concentrated** desk deliberately: a roster of only diversified strategies produces a suspiciously narrow spread, and real fields have blowups. Fill-to-target-field-size so desks taper as real entrants arrive, plus a kill switch and exclusion from every real-user metric (joining the existing CR035-synthetics filter) — a desk must never inflate a number Saiful uses to decide. **Eligibility clause (Saiful: *"we can say that employees and the family of AMI Trading cannot win awards etc"*, then *"you are 'my employee' at this time"* — which collapses it into one rule rather than a list):** **anything operated by, employed by, or affiliated with AMI Trading may rank, but may not hold a title, champion reward or permanent flair.** Four instances of that single principle — house desks (entrants the company operates), the operator himself and staff/admin, household and immediate family, and test/UAT/seed accounts (the Hermes rig on melehost drives a real device and its runs can enter fields). Needed **independently of the desks**, because the operator plays: *"2026 Annual Champion: Saiful"* is a problem whether or not he earned it, and a competition whose operator can win its own prizes looks rigged even when it isn't — which strengthens `competition_rules.md` §8's skill-vs-chance footing. **Ineligible ≠ invisible, and that distinction is the point:** they enter, trade and rank, the board shows what actually happened, and only the *title* passes down to the highest eligible entrant — stated plainly (*"Title: SLATE_07 (2nd overall)"*) rather than silently renumbering, since a board that quietly promotes second place looks like a bug while one that explains itself looks like a rule. This is also what avoids the tell: no hidden exclusion to notice. Scope is deliberately narrow — career points still accrue, so the operator can dogfood progression and desks still populate a meaningful spread. Belongs in **`competition_rules.md` v2.0**, the document with standing, which §15 already re-versions for the P&L change. **Forward dependency: if credits are ever paid on a P&L outcome, operator and staff participation stops being hygiene and becomes load-bearing** — same lawyer review. **FINAL REVIEW** ([final_review.md](CR109_pnl_game_ami_cash/final_review.md)), covering Saiful's last three asks — *"make this addictive… remind them to play… players will be a source of income if they view adverts… enable the social aspect, they can discuss trades and give tips"* — each of which collides with something already decided. **ADS: the trap that would break §15.** The compliance position rests on **consideration absent** (free entry) + **prize absent** (cosmetic, non-purchasable); **rewarded video — the standard mobile pattern — attacks the consideration leg**, and every natural ad-funded mechanic is fatal: *"watch an ad to restart"* makes restart purchasable with attention, *"watch an ad for a second entry"* also breaks §4.1's one-run-per-cadence farm guard, *"watch an ad for extra AMI Cash"* is money buying Stake. Non-monetary consideration counts. **New invariant: no ad may ever be required, rewarded, or gate anything** — not entry, re-entry, restart, capital, information, timing, or cosmetics that double as competition rewards. **The §3.1 one-way rule catches all of them unaided**, the clearest evidence yet that the three-layer model is load-bearing rather than descriptive. Ads therefore run as **ambient inventory on non-contest surfaces** (lobby, Record, app open) — never the board, never the trade ticket, and **never the Close**, since an ad in the trophy moment cheapens the one emotional payoff the period arc exists to deliver; the game monetises **indirectly** by driving sessions. **No ad infrastructure exists** (no SDK, units, mediation or consent flow — "Floor Pass" is a tier name, not an implementation), so ads are **their own CR** and must not be entangled with this schedule. **RETENTION: remind on events that need a decision, never on events that only invite watching** — entries closing / run closing / a challenge received / results ready / dropped out of the top 10 *once per run*, but never "your position moved". Not restraint for its own sake: **the cheap notification costs the valuable one**, because push fatigue makes users disable the channel that delivers the Close. Caps ≤1/day, ≤4/week, quiet hours; lands on the same side as §10's *one beat per market close, never per tick*. **SOCIAL: the app has zero UGC today** — the only user-authored value is the system-generated handle, and there is **no report, no block, no profanity filter, no moderation tooling** anywhere in the repo. **Apple Guideline 1.2 requires four things of any UGC app** (filter, report, block, published contact with **action within 24 hours**) — a standing daily obligation for a one-person team, and the real cost of the feature; an unmoderated stock-tip channel is also the highest-risk UGC category (pump schemes, "DM me for signals" funnels, unlicensed advice on a platform not licensed to give investment advice, and AR/MS content Saiful cannot personally moderate). Phased **A → B → C**: structured reactions (fixed vocabulary, **no moderation surface at all**), then **post-close rationale notes on your own already-closed trades** — the safest reading of "discuss trades" because it is structurally **retrospective** (never a signal), **scoped to your own trades** (never a generic tip channel), **length-capped** and **attached to a real scored decision** (analysis, not opinion) — then open discussion only with a moderation budget that does not exist. **The "tips" itch is already largely served**: the strategy desks publish their rules, and the 12 agents are a licensed-safe, moderation-free way to comment on a closed field. **AMENDMENT D — the independent review fold-in.** Saiful commissioned a review series (`AT:Fable`, five documents: [psychology_review.md](CR109_pnl_game_ami_cash/psychology_review.md) F1–F9, [comparative_review.md](CR109_pnl_game_ami_cash/comparative_review.md) C1–C6, [trade_execution_addendum.md](CR109_pnl_game_ami_cash/trade_execution_addendum.md) the fee + G1–G3, [playability_addendum.md](CR109_pnl_game_ami_cash/playability_addendum.md) the lab framing + L1–L6, [review_synthesis.md](CR109_pnl_game_ami_cash/review_synthesis.md) S1–S10) *"before I commit to a HUGE development cost"*; the series deliberately left CR109.md unedited so the design keeps one author, and this amendment applies it. **Every item's disposition is in §20.** **Two rulings from Saiful.** (1) **The PDT-style day-trade rule is REJECTED; the escalator is held in reserve** — the review framed a 3-round-trips-per-5-days cap as *"realism, not restriction"*, but PDT is a **broker constraint on one account type** (a cash account isn't subject to it), so it fails the bar market-hours and trading-costs clear, and the addendum proposing it opens *"nothing below caps what a player may do"* then caps what a player may do two sections later. The FPL-style escalator (first N fills at base cost, beyond N at 3×) achieves the same anti-scalping goal by **pricing rather than prohibiting**, which is the doctrine. (2) **The agent post-mortem SHIPS, for paying customers only** — amending *"Games is only about trade"* at the close boundary only (the agents stay out of the run itself, which is what that decision protected). It gives the game a direct revenue line that never touches the ad invariant, and puts the strongest upsell in the product at peak attention. **Four fences:** free players keep the **entire** Close (rank, delta, curve, both counterfactual lines — nothing removed to manufacture the upsell, or the peak-end payoff becomes a paywall and the re-entry keystone dies for the half of the base that funds ad revenue); the locked card lives in the **debrief panel, never inside the three-beat ceremony**; retrospective-only is **structural** — a fixed template filled from computed run data, not a prompt instruction (CR038: agents ignore emphatic instructions ~70% of the time); and **no paid feature may alter a run's inputs, scoring or ranking** (§3.1.1 — post-close explanation is the entire permitted surface for plan tier, and the lawyer sees this paragraph rather than discovering it). **FOUR CORRECTIONS TO THE REVIEW, made as its recipient.** (1) **F1 understates itself.** The review found the median player's Record flatlines — placement is zero-sum, so a player oscillating between the 40th and 60th percentile nets ≈0 per run forever (p=0.60→+8.9, p=0.45→−4) and the 500-point first title never arrives. Correct, but §6.5 clamped the **headline**, not the ledger — so the player carries an **invisible debt** (signed total −30, earns +8, screen doesn't move) and when it does move it moves on a ≈zero-drift walk, which is **variable-ratio reinforcement on a status number** — the exact pattern the review's own dark-pattern register marks *never*. **Fix: clamp the ledger at write time**, so `SUM(delta)` is always the displayed number. The wound itself is fixed by a **finish stipend** (~5/weekly finish, guarded on entered + ≥1 trade + not forfeited + held to close, so it can't become a check-in). (2) **S1 and S2 are one mechanism, and it taxes the wrong cohort.** The fee is scoring-**neutral** under placement (everyone in the field pays it, ranks unchanged) and scoring-**negative** under the benchmark (the index pays nothing) — and thin fields route to the benchmark, so the fee **systematically penalises the alpha-window cohort and stops penalising anyone once fields clear n≥8**: same skill, worse score, decided by join date. Fixed by scoring against the **achievable benchmark** (SPY net of the one entry fee a player would pay to hold it — runs end marked not liquidated, so it's one fill) while the Close still **displays** the gross comparison, which is the game's best line: *"the index pays no fees. You beat it anyway"* — the reason most active managers underperform, discovered in the player's own numbers. (3) **F5's arithmetic contradicts F1's.** A 100-point first rung at a 5-point stipend is **twenty finishes** — five months, worse than the problem; raising the stipend instead breaks its own anti-farm guard. **Fix: the first rung is a milestone — 3 finished runs, none forfeited** — reachable in three weeks, unfarmable because it fires once, and it removes a tuning constant instead of adding one. (4) **C1 reopens F1's wound.** Points-capped private fields give zero progression to players in the genre's most retentive mode. **Fix: placement points capped, finish stipend still pays** — placement is rank-dependent so alts can farm it; the stipend is rank-dependent on nothing, so no arrangement between accounts can conjure one. **ACCEPTED FROM THE SERIES.** **The trading cost** (Saiful: *"we have to have some fee attached to the trade… so that 'spray and pray', while may still work, is not the preferred strategy"*) — 10 bps of notional, min 1.00 AMI Cash, per fill, both sides, **burned never pooled** (a pool is a wagered stake and §15's prize leg dies), game path only, desks pay identical costs, **not a capital event** so it doesn't break the TWR chain. bps handles churning big, the minimum handles spraying dust. **Queue-first is promoted to a primary design principle** — US regular hours are **evening in the Gulf and past midnight in Malaysia**, so for the target markets placing orders outside market hours is what most players do most of the time: *plan the book tonight, fills at the open, the morning card reports what filled*. The **3-tap ticket** (watchlist chips → size chips with 25% as the visual default → confirm card showing est. cost and book-percentage), with stop/target presets that are nearly free (`submit()` already accepts them and `evaluate_outcomes()` already watches them) and teach plan-the-exit-at-entry. **The alpha→points formula, which existed in no document** despite being the default path for months at alpha field sizes: same 2.5:1 asymmetry as placement, clamped at ±1 so no alpha outcome outpays winning a field. **The Close gets a ceremony budget of three beats** — the series had attached eleven blocks to the one screen whose entire job is a single emotional payoff, so: the result, **one** insight chosen by priority, the way back in; everything else one tap deeper in a debrief panel. **Entry stays one screen, three taps** for the same reason from the other end. **The re-entry CTA is the final beat** of both Close and Wind-Up, and `close → re-entry` + `first-run activation` are instrumented from day one as the game's health metrics. **The first run is always a duel against the Index Desk** — a routing rule over machinery already planned, giving a guaranteed opponent at n=1 real players, a guaranteed narrative (*you beat the market* or *the market beat you*, both stories), and bounded difficulty for a beginner's first unbounded stock-pick. **Private fields with a join code** — the largest gap the comparison found: two decades of paper-trading competitions and season-long fantasy run on the **private league**, not the public board, and every competitive surface here faced strangers. **The PR board** (best weekly TWR, best alpha, best drawdown control, longest hold, longest streak) — the only competitive surface that **works at n=1**, which is precisely the alpha condition. **A rolling skill stat** on the Record (trailing-N alpha or Sharpe) because career points confound skill with volume and never answer *am I getting better* — it can fall, which is what makes it credible, and it never gates anything. **The streak gets a bye week** (Duolingo's freeze — a long streak's loss becomes a churn cliff). **The mirrors** (lab framing, Saiful: *"this is where you try things and go wild, and see that the wider you go, the less likely you are to make money"*): intent tag, wildness index, two counterfactual lines at every close (*"if you'd held your first picks untouched: +2.1%"*, *"if you'd just held the S&P: +0.6%"*), a live book-heat gauge, and opt-in challenge cards that pay **markers, never points**. All **private** — asserted at the serializer — because billboarding them turns self-knowledge into performance. **This inverts the D-060 objection:** the game doesn't teach gambling psychology, it **falsifies it with the player's own data**. **Attribution on the daily beat** (*"NVDA drove +1.9% of your +2.3%"*) because a no-rules weekly arena is substantially luck and players who sense outcomes aren't contingent on their decisions stop playing — learned helplessness is the churn nobody exit-surveys. **Near-miss framing points up only, never at a loss** (the slot-machine pattern). **Three engine gaps formalised:** dividends unmodelled (so the benchmark is **price-only** to match, with crediting before Q/H/Y — the Dividend Desk is otherwise handicapped by its entire yield), splits unhandled (adjust quantity and basis in place, flag the row, **no TWR break** — a 4:1 split otherwise craters a scored run), and quote freshness (measure Yahoo's lag on melehost before any board is live; the fee raised the exploit's bar to ~20 bps per round trip, so it's due diligence rather than urgent). **All twelve scoring constants move into `games_scoring.py`**, each with a loud test, and §18's tuning list is **generated from it** rather than maintained by hand across five documents. **Staged funding with evidence gates** — Stage 1 (the addictive core: slices 1–3c plus the above) is roughly a third of the plan and contains every hook that matters; **Gate 1** (activation + re-entry meeting targets Saiful sets **before** the build, so it can't be argued backwards from the data) precedes funding slice 4; **Gate 2** (fields clearing n≥8 organically, title rungs being crossed) precedes Q/H/Y, cosmetics and roadmap modes — because **status systems only pay once there is a crowd to hold status in**, and the crowd is built by the cheap loop. **The one-way rule survived intact** — ~40 additions across five documents and not one crosses it, which is the third time §3 has caught a problem unaided. **New risk registered:** paid coaching on a scored board is a **perception** risk even though it is not pay-to-win — two players enter on identical terms and only one is coached afterwards; the mitigation is that the free Close is complete and the boast the game is built around (*beat the market*) needs no subscription to earn. Adds a new user-facing string set — `retranslate:[ar,ms]`. **AMENDMENT F — THE DARK LAUNCH (2026-08-09). This is the amendment that starts the build.** Saiful: *"We have a CR dedicated towards a games engine for the app. I want to start developing it but I do not want to incorporate it into the app just yet, or at least I do not want the users to be able to play it yet."* Two options evaluated — **a separate app** or **hidden access inside AMI Trade** — and he took the second. **Why not a separate app:** the repo has one Flutter package and one bundle ID (`ai.agenticmarketintel.amiTrade`), and the game reuses auth, AMI Cash, quotes, the design system, the API client, i18n, RevenueCat and OneSignal — so a second app either duplicates `mobile/lib/services/` + `mobile/lib/theme/` or forces a shared-package refactor across the tree; it adds a permanent per-release tax (second store record, provisioning, listings, privacy labels, review cycle, and `build_testflight.sh`/`publish_playstore.sh`/`install_iphone.sh` all assume one app); it needs cross-app identity because career points belong to the AMI Trade account; and it is thrown away when the game ships in-app. **Decisively, it does not isolate the half that carries the risk** — the game shares users, AMI Cash, Postgres and market data, so the schema, the migrations and the §7.1 `sim_engine.submit()` split land in the live Alpha stack either way. Saiful then added *"the main app will continue to be developed at the same time"*, which strengthens the ruling rather than complicating it: a fork of the design system would diverge daily instead of costing once. **Four rulings.** (1) **The gate is compile-time, on the client, and it is the ONLY gate.** `bool.fromEnvironment('AMI_GAMES')` guards a const-conditional entry in `mobile/lib/app.dart`'s `routes:` map — the `/dev-preview` pattern already shipped in the app, a registered route with no UI entry point anywhere — so **no distributed binary contains a reachable route**. Structural rather than a runtime flag, because App Review guideline 2.3.1 names hidden/undocumented features and CR040's doctrine is that a switch someone can flip is not a control. Saiful **rejected** a server-side kill switch and user allowlist — *"why bother? so long as no one can reach it, the additional control adds complication with no upside"* — and he is right: a `GAMES_ENABLED` pinned `true` for the entire dark phase is a config line, not a control, and an allowlist adds parsing, compose-parity surface and tests to guard against a user who cannot get there. **One consequence still needed handling, and not with a control:** `main.py` sets `docs_url="/docs" if settings.env != "prod" else None` with `openapi_url` left at default, so on Alpha both `/docs` and `/openapi.json` serve — registering the games router would **publish** the entire API with schemas, converting "nobody knows the paths" into "the paths are indexed". Fixed where it happens: the router registers with **`include_in_schema=False`**. One kwarg, no env setting, no `docker-compose.yml` forwarding, no allowlist. **Residual accepted:** an already-authenticated alpha user who independently guesses an unpublished path could call it; population small and known, paths unadvertised, and the `field_id` cleanup handle covers it. (2) **Both platforms** — *"I have IOS and Android devices, so both build are needed"*; `scripts/install_iphone.sh` and `scripts/install_android.sh` already thread dart-defines and each gains `--dart-define=AMI_GAMES=1`, while `build_testflight.sh`/`build_playstore.sh` are untouched so store binaries carry no games route. (3) **Dark play writes the REAL ledger** — *"real from day 1. we will need history anyway, and we can always clean the data"* — so **no `is_internal` column**; §4.5's `career_events` already carries `field_id` and `entry_id`, making cleanup a field-scoped delete, **which holds only if the scoring pass never writes a row with either null — now an acceptance assertion in slice 3**. (4) **CR133 NO LONGER BLOCKS CR109** — *"if we are building it into the same current app at this phase, we can unblock it"*; §13.1's objection was that the game would ship with nowhere to live, and the hidden route is a temporary home, so CR133 stays deferred and untouched and the game re-homes into the real nav when CR133 ships. **This reverses the "depends on CR133 and must be developed with it" clause above.** **Build scope opened: slices 1, 2 and 3 only** — slice 1 is ungated (it ships the equity curve to the *training* portfolio and has no game surface at all); 3b/3c and beyond are a separate decision after Saiful has played it. **Amendment G (2026-08-11) — shorting, at 0.3%.** Saiful, playing the shipped build: *"the game does not allow 'short' selling? we will need to add a 'fee' for short selling. lets set it at 0.3% for now."* Reverses §5.1's *"Long only. A hook that refused any `git checkout` of a dirty file would be the stronger control and is deliberately not built here, because it would fight legitimate use. | CR114 | 2026-07-29 | **Q7 asks for exclusions and offers inclusions — regroup its chips under ONLY / NEVER headers.** Saiful, bug report `b5a5e923` (Platinum Anchor, `0.1.0+57`): *"this question as asking for an exclusion. but halal and ESG are inclusion responses. maybe we need to split inclusion and exclusion questions."* Confirmed at [`concierge_engine.py:112-124`](../../../backend/app/services/concierge_engine.py#L112-L124): the question is *"Anything I should know about what you'd **NEVER** want to invest in? The rest are a different kind of rule entirely: `Halal only` and `ESG-leaning` are **inclusion filters** (invest only within a screened universe), `Long-only (no shorting)` is a **strategy constraint**, `Liquid only (no microcaps)` a **liquidity floor**. Verify both at 1.0 and 1.15 text scale in AR before calling it done. `retranslate:[ar,ms]` — the two new header strings plus any chip label touched. Relates to **CR036 §3** (the halal positioning this protects), **DEF060** (why the flow is not lengthened), **DEF129** (Q8, the adjacent interview step being removed in the same file). **BUILT 2026-07-29 (AT:R65), in one pass with DEF129 since both edit the same question block.** `Q7_TEXT` now asks for both directions — *"Any hard rules I should hand your analysts? ONLY narrows where they can invest; NEVER puts something off the table entirely"* — and each chip carries its own direction rather than relying on a header: `ONLY halal / Sharia-compliant`, `ONLY ESG-leaning`, `ONLY liquid names (no microcaps)`, `ONLY long positions (no shorting)`, `NEVER tobacco, alcohol or gambling`, `NEVER fossil fuels`, `No hard rules`. **Per-chip prefixes rather than the grouped ONLY/NEVER headers the spec proposed:** the chip list is a flat array the client renders as tappable pills, so a header row would either be a tappable non-answer or a client-side change — and the whole point of doing this server-side was that it reaches already-installed builds. Same information, no new ARB ids, no release needed. **The guard is a chip→flag contract test, and it is the part worth keeping.** The chip a user taps IS the string `_parse_constraints` sees, and nothing links the two — that is exactly why this defect survived: rewording a chip silently produces a mandate that ignores the tap, and every existing test passed throughout. The new test taps each chip **exactly as shipped** and asserts the compliance flags that come back, one flag per chip, no spillover. It carries a **vacuity guard** (`set(Q7_CHIPS) == set(_CHIP_TO_FLAG)`) because without it, adding a chip would leave the assertion loops iterating a stale table — passing while testing nothing — and a reachability check that every boolean compliance flag is settable from some chip, since a flag no chip can raise is a rule the interview cannot capture. **Mutations, all measured: (1)** reword `ONLY long positions (no shorting)` → `ONLY long positions` (losing the parser's `no short` token) → vacuity guard RED; **(2)** drop the `"no short"` clause from `_parse_constraints` while leaving the chips untouched → contract test RED, which is the sharper case since the chip list still looks correct; **(3)** add `ONLY dividend payers` with no table entry → vacuity guard RED. **Backend 1589 green.** No mandate data was ever corrupted (the parser keys off substrings and set the right flags regardless), so this shipped as copy + IA with the contract test as the durable half. | done | — | AT:R65 |

| CR117 | 2026-07-29 | **The app's "hexagons" are octagons — add a real hexagon clipper, migrate the controls that should be hexagonal, and stop the class name lying.** Saiful, bug report `589e7607` (Platinum Anchor, `0.1.0+57`), on the ticker period toggle: *"the buttons are octagonal, not hexagonal."* **Correct, and the code already admits it.** [`hex_clipper.dart:11-14`](../../../mobile/lib/theme/hex_clipper.dart#L11-L14) declares `class FlatTopHexagonClipper` whose own docstring reads *"Cut-corner octagon — what the design system spec calls a 'hex clip-path'"*, and `getClip` emits an **8-point path**: it cuts all four corners of the rect, producing two angled ends **plus** angled top and bottom. A flat-top hexagon has six sides — angled ends, flat top and bottom — which is exactly what the sibling `FlatTopRegularHexagon` (:47) draws for agent avatars and the honeycomb. **So the app ships two different shapes under one name**, and every "hex" *control* is an octagon: `HexButton`, `HexChip`, `GlassPanel` accents, `ticker_chart.dart:185`'s period toggle, and the BOARD segment of the Room toggle. Only the avatars and honeycomb are genuinely hexagonal. On a small chip the difference is subliminal; on the wide, saturated, selected period pill in the screenshot it is unmistakable, which is why this surfaced on the toggle first. **This reframes DEF146 and is the reason it cannot ship without this CR.** The AT:Designer's toggle (`df515c35`) is a **true hexagon** — angled cuts on the outer edges only, flat top and bottom, straight internal divider. That shape is **not producible** by `FlatTopHexagonClipper` at any `cornerCut`, so DEF146's fix was mis-scoped as "apply the same clipper to both halves"; it needs the new path this CR builds. **RULED (Saiful, 2026-07-29 0900 check-in): "Add a real hexagon clipper, migrate controls to it."** Rejected: rename-only (leaves DEF146 unbuildable) and a two-shape rule with no principle for choosing. **Scope:** (1) add a true flat-top hexagon path for *rect-proportioned* controls — note this is **not** `FlatTopRegularHexagon`, which is locked to a 2:√3 bounding box and will not stretch to a button's aspect ratio without distorting the angle; the new clipper takes a corner inset and cuts only the left and right edges. (2) Migrate the controls that should read as hexagonal, **starting with the DEF146 toggle**, which is the one with a signed-off design. (3) **Rename `FlatTopHexagonClipper` to what it is** (`CutCornerOctagonClipper` or similar) — the name has misled every reader since it was written, including the CR106 spec work that reasoned about "hex geometry" on controls that have none. **Deliberately open, to be decided during the work rather than guessed here:** which of the remaining controls become true hexagons and which stay octagons. Do **not** sweep them all — the octagon has shipped for months and reads as intentional; migrate on evidence (a design, or a report like this one), not on tidiness. Note **CR113** removes the shape from large CTAs entirely, so those are out of scope here, and **CR108** edits `TrackHexButton`, which already uses the true-hexagon clipper and must not be caught in the migration. Update `ami_hex_in_flutter.md` alongside CR113's rule so the two shapes and their uses are documented in one place. Relates to **DEF146** (blocked on this), **CR113** (removes octagons from CTAs), **CR106 §4.0** (reasoned about "hex" controls that are octagons), **CR108** (adjacent, must not be swept).  **DELIVERED (AT:R65, 2026-07-29) — the mechanical half, in full; the open design question left open as the CR directed.** Built ahead of CR120 rather than beside it, because CR120's segmented tabs are specified as *"hex-clipped, `cornerCut: 8`, matching `ticker_chart.dart:185`"* — one of the twelve call sites this CR renames. Laning them in parallel would have had CR120 build its tabs in the octagon this CR exists to stop, on an identifier being renamed underneath it. **(1) The true hexagon: `FlatTopHexagonBarClipper`** — angled ends, flat top and bottom, six sides, free `endInset` so it holds its angle at any aspect ratio. Confirmed by measurement that neither existing class could do the job: `CutCornerOctagonClipper` cuts the top and bottom at every `cornerCut`, and `FlatTopRegularHexagon`'s diagonals start at a fixed `w * 0.25`, so on a 200×40 bar it flattens into a near-triangle — a point 40pt in from the end is inside the new bar's flat top and outside the regular hexagon's, which is pinned as a test. **(2) The rename: 12 sites across 9 files**, `FlatTopHexagonClipper` → `CutCornerOctagonClipper`. **The new class deliberately did NOT inherit the vacated name**, which is the one judgement call here: it is what the name always claimed, but had it taken it, any unmigrated call site — or one written in a lane in flight, which is precisely the situation CR120 creates — would keep compiling and *silently change shape*. Because `FlatTopHexagonClipper` now names nothing, a stale reference is a **compile error instead of a wrong shape**: CLAUDE.md's degrade-loudly rule applied to a rename. **(3) DEF146 migrated and thereby closed** (see its row). **The guard counts sides**, which is the property the name makes a claim about and the one nothing checked: `getBounds` is identical for all three clippers, which is exactly why an octagon shipped under a hexagon's name for months. The test walks the path, recovers its vertices from direction changes, and asserts 8 / 6 / 6. *(Its first version reported 7 and 5 — the walk skipped the corner sitting on the path's seam. Fixed to be cyclic; noted because a shape guard that is quietly one side short is worse than none.)* Plus a **name guard** that fails if the old identifier is reintroduced as a compatibility alias, matching it in **code position only** so the docstring that explains the rename does not trip it — with its own vacuity check that the regex can still see a violation. **Two mutations independently RED:** give the hexagon bar cut top and bottom (i.e. make it an octagon again); reintroduce `typedef FlatTopHexagonClipper = CutCornerOctagonClipper` and point a call site at it. Mobile **251** (was 243), `flutter analyze` exit 0, same 5 pre-existing infos. `ami_hex_in_flutter.md` now carries a three-shape table, the reason the old name is gone, and the migrate-on-evidence rule. **Left open exactly as the CR asked:** which remaining controls become true hexagons. Nothing was swept — the octagon has shipped for months and reads as intentional; `TrackHexButton` (CR108) and the large CTAs (CR113) are untouched by design. **Client-only, rides the `+58` batch.** | done | — | AT:R65 |

Also give the capped list a visible affordance that it scrolls (a fade or partial row at the cut) — a list that is clipped with no cue reads as a rendering bug, which is how this same pattern produced clipped-CTA reports under **DEF075**. **BUILT 2026-07-29 (AT:R65).** Mine to build rather than the CR120 lane's: this was folded in as that lane's **acceptance 11** by amendment `ba0aa979`, which landed *after* the worker branched at `2f49e350`, and `claude -p` is one-shot — so the lane never saw the requirement. Verified absent by grep before building, and **not a finding against the builder**. **Shape:** the legend is a **fixed**-height viewport, not a maximum, so the card's footprint is constant whatever the allocation; rows carry a fixed **22pt** extent so *"does this scroll"* is arithmetic rather than text measurement, which is the only reason the boundary is testable at all. **One deliberate deviation from this row, stated rather than quietly taken:** it asks for "approximately the donut's height" (72pt) and the build uses **99pt (4.5 rows)**. At 3.5 rows the number would be 77 and much closer, but it would make **the reporter's own four-sector portfolio start scrolling** — a present regression for the person who filed a forward-looking request. 4.5 rows leaves every typical allocation static and still bounds the card; the boundary is 5+ sectors. **The half-row at the cut is the affordance**, with a `ShaderMask` bottom fade over it, and **both appear only when something is actually hidden** — a fade with nothing behind it is a lie, and this row is explicit that a list clipped with no cue reads as a rendering bug (the **DEF075** shape). **Both nested-scrollable traps this row names are handled:** the list has its **own `ScrollController`** (without one it attaches to the inherited `PrimaryScrollController` and drives the outer view instead of itself) and uses **`NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` when the content fits**, so a legend with nothing to scroll cannot swallow a drag meant for the screen. **Guard: 5 tests, measured against the 13-sector fixture this row demands, not the reporter's four** — and read off the render tree with `getSize` rather than asserting a widget exists, because *"it is capped"* is a claim about **height**, and a `shrinkWrap` list would satisfy a widget-existence check while silently re-expanding to full content height. The footprint test carries its own non-vacuity check (fade absent at 4, present at 13) so *"the height did not change"* cannot pass on two identical renders, and one test exists purely to prove **nothing is lost behind the cap**: scroll to the tail and the 12th sector really is there while the first has really gone. **Mutations measured:** removing the fixed height and adding `shrinkWrap: true` → **3 RED**; dropping the fade → **2 RED**; making the list always scrollable → **1 RED**. **Found while writing the tests:** pumping the same widget types twice reuses the element tree, so Riverpod served the *previous* allocation for a frame and the 4-sector case was silently asserting against 13-sector state — it presented as a genuine failure; the harness now tears the tree down between pumps. Mobile 284 green at commit (299 after the same day's DEF151/DEF139/DEF156 pass), `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos` exit 0. **CR116 was dropped** (superseded by CR120's tabs), so the "sequence them in one pass" note below is moot. Note **CR116** reorders this screen's sections in the same file; sequence them in one pass. Relates to **CR119** (the broader redesign this anticipates), **CR116** (same file, same lane), **DEF075** (clipped-content-without-affordance precedent). **FOLDED INTO [CR120](CR120_portfolio_list_structure/CR120.md) (Saiful, 2026-07-29), and dispatched into that lane as Amendment 1 while it was already running.** The Architect had recommended *holding* this until CR120 integrated; Saiful overruled, and the overrule is the better call — **CR120 moves this donut into the Positions tab**, so the lane worker is the one holding its new home, and a follow-up would have been specified against a layout that no longer exists. Delivered as CR120 **acceptance 11**: constant card height at 4 sectors and at 13, legend scrolling within its own bounds, visible affordance at the cut. This row's implementation note went across **verbatim**, because that note is the whole value of the item — an unbounded nested `ListView` throws and a `shrinkWrap` one *silently re-expands to full content height*, which looks correct in a 4-sector fixture and regresses the moment someone diversifies — with one correction: **the container is no longer the top-level `ListView` at `:137`** that the note was written against, so the nesting must be re-read before the height is bounded. **Caveat recorded honestly:** `claude -p` is one-shot, so if the worker had already read its assign file the amendment is invisible to it; the Architect verifies acceptance 11 at integration and builds it there if absent. **CR116, which this row said to sequence in the same pass, was dropped** — CR120 supersedes it. | done | — | AT:R65 |
| CR119 | 2026-07-29 | **Portfolio screen redesign — watchlist, holdings and trades all grow without bound; commission AT:Design.** Saiful, bug report `9d51ce11` (Platinum Anchor, `0.1.0+57`): *"in Portfolio, the watchlist, holding and trades will all increase in numbers. we need a better way to view them. we need a AT:Design to work on this."* Filed as a **design commission**, not an implementation CR — the instruction names the owner, so no solution is proposed here and none should be inferred from this row. **The structural problem, stated so the designer has the constraints rather than the symptom.** [`portfolio_screen.dart:137-160`](../../../mobile/lib/screens/sim/portfolio_screen.dart#L137-L160) is a single top-level `ListView` whose children are laid out in full: `_ValueCard` → `_SectorAllocationSection` → `_WatchlistSection` → the holdings block (one `_HoldingCard` per position) → the trades block. **Three of those five are unbounded**, and every one of them grows through exactly the behaviour the product is trying to teach — watch more tickers, hold more positions, trade more often. A user the app has succeeded with is a user whose portfolio screen is unusable. Today's reporter sits at 89.3% cash with 4 sector rows and a short list, so nothing is broken yet; this is a scaling ceiling, filed before it is hit. **Interactions the design has to absorb, all decided today and all in this file:** **CR116** moves holdings above the watchlist, **CR118** caps and scrolls the sector legend, and CR116's row flags that the holdings block is a conditional (`if (p.holdings.isEmpty)` renders `_NewTraderHint`), so the empty state is a distinct layout, not a degenerate case of the populated one. A redesign that ignores the empty state will regress the new-trader experience DEF060 exists to protect. Also live in this screen: `_watchlistKey`, a `GlobalKey` used as a scroll/coach-mark target, which any restructure must keep attached. **Open questions for the design, not for this row:** whether the three lists become tabs, sections with independent scroll, or separate screens; what the summary state of a collapsed list shows (count? top holding? total value?); and whether trades — the least-referenced and fastest-growing of the three — belongs on this screen at all rather than behind the Journal, which is already the durable record surface. **Sequencing:** CR116 and CR118 are small, ruled and land first; they are not blocked on this and should not wait for it. This CR stays `proposed` until AT:Design delivers, at which point it gets a spec folder and a normal build lane. Precedent for the handoff: **DEF146**, where the Designer's output arrived as a bug-report attachment and became the normative source for the fix. **CLOSED (Saiful, 2026-07-29): the commission was delivered same-day as [CR120](CR120_portfolio_list_structure/CR120.md).** AT:Design built and measured all four candidate structures on identical data in a live prototype — today's screen, segmented tabs, a bounded dashboard and collapsible sections — read scroll extents out of the DOM at 390×844 rather than estimating, and Saiful chose **segmented tabs** (heavy profile: 25.4 screens today → 2.9–4.2 across three tabs, worst reachable 4.2). CR120 also answered two of the three open questions this row posed: **trades stay on this screen** — the design found the premise *"users can still check trades in the Journal"* is **half false**, since Floor Pass gets 30-day journal retention while `sim_trades` has none, so for a free user the Portfolio is the **durable** record and the Journal the lossy one; and the collapsed-summary question dissolved, since a tab shows its **count** in the label, which is what tells a user the other two are not empty. The empty state and `_watchlistKey` warnings carried forward into the build lane. This row closes as **done** because its deliverable was a design, and the design exists; the implementation is tracked as CR120. | done | [CR120_portfolio_list_structure/](CR120_portfolio_list_structure/) | AT:R65 |
| CR120 | 2026-07-29 | **Portfolio: structure for three growing lists, and a cap on trade history.** Saiful: *"The portfolio screen has watchlist, holdings and trade history. They will all grow. We need a better way than simple scrolling one after another. We also need to limit the trades to either a number of items… or of a period… Users can still check trades in the Journal instead."* **Measured, from the DOM of a built prototype at 390×844, not estimated:** `portfolio_screen.dart:137` is a `ListView(children:)` — **not `.builder`** — so every row is constructed on every rebuild, and since `TradeRow`/`_WatchlistRow` are `ConsumerWidget`s under a `ref.watch(simNotifierProvider)`, a price tick rebuilds all of them: **3.6 screens / 31 rows** at a modest account, **8.9 / 84** at six months, **25.4 / 252** at heavy use. Growth is linear and unbounded because nothing is capped server-side either — `sim_engine.py:447 list_trades` selects every trade the user has ever made, `opened_at DESC`, no `limit`, no `offset`. **Three structural findings shaped the fix.** (1) **Open and closed trades are interleaved by open date** — there is no status split in the render path (`:170`), so a live position opened in April sits below forty closed trades from May; **open trades are money at risk, not history, and are never capped in any option**. (2) **The watchlist is not user-curated — it auto-grows**: `sim.py:302` silently adds every traded ticker and `watchlist_store.add` has no cap, so the same ticker can appear in all three sections without the user ever touching it. (3) The sector donut renders above the watchlist today and reads as unrelated to anything; it belongs inside Holdings. **The premise needed correcting, and the correction is binding.** *"Users can still check trades in the Journal"* is **half true**: every trade does write a journal entry carrying the full trade JSON (`sim.py:314`, `:393`, `:446`) and the Journal already ships a TRADE filter chip plus search — **but Floor Pass gets 30-day retention** (`journal_store.py:42-47`, `FLOOR_PASS_RETENTION_DAYS = 30`) while `sim_trades` has none. For a free user the relationship is **inverted — the Portfolio is the durable record and the Journal is the lossy one** — so a fetch-limit cap pointing at the Journal would silently delete their own trade history from every surface (CR040, degrade loudly, with the user's data as the thing lost). **That one line is the entire plan-dependent surface of the screen** — verified, not assumed: not a single `plan` reference in `sim.py` or `watchlist.py`, and no plan-gated limit anywhere in the sim path (`credit_service`/`reputation_service` hold the only plan gates and neither touches the Portfolio), so Floor Pass vs Trader is one caveat appearing or not, beneath the action it qualifies — deliberate placement, since a user does not need to know about Journal retention until they are about to rely on the Journal, but it does make the difference invisible from the landing tab. **THE CLIENT MUST NOT BRANCH ON PLAN — it branches on `retention_days`.** Saiful, seeing the toggle: *"So a slightly different UI depending on plan."* Yes, but not implemented as one, and the distinction is load-bearing: the Journal list response already carries `retention_days`, the client already parses it (`journal.dart:141` → `JournalState.retentionDays`), and **the Journal screen already renders an amber notice from it** (`journal_screen.dart:113-120`) — so CR120 is **extending a shipped disclosure to the screen that links to it**, not inventing a pattern (reinventing it would be DEF098's two-renderer class on a monetisation-adjacent string), and the UI branches on *"is there a retention window?"* — an integer, or `null` for unlimited, computed server-side. No plan state to sync, no wrong-branch risk from a stale client idea of the plan, and a policy change reaches users without a release. **Never hardcode 30 in the app.** **Fail-safe:** `retention_days` today only arrives on the journal list response, which the Portfolio never calls, so if it is unknown the Portfolio shows the caveat **without a number** and never the reassuring branch — a spurious warning is recoverable, a missing one is the thing the section exists to prevent (CR040); **B3** (`journal_retention_days` on the sim portfolio/trades response) removes the guess. **NOTHING IS DELETED — AND THE SHIPPED STRING SAYS OTHERWISE.** Writing the honest version exposed a defect in the one already live: `journalRetentionWarning` reads *"Floor Pass: last {days} days only. Upgrade to keep everything."* but **retention is a read-time filter** (`journal_store.py:134-136` appends `where created_at >= cutoff` to the select; the only `delete(JournalEntryRow)` in the store is a test-only `clear()`), so an entry outside the window is hidden, not destroyed, and reappears on upgrade — and for sim trades it is doubly wrong, since `sim_trades` has no retention at all. *"Upgrade to **keep** everything"* asserts a data loss that is not happening in order to drive a purchase, in shipped user-facing copy on a paid-conversion surface: CR038/DEF059's confident-wrongness family. Fix is one verb (*keep* → *see*) plus a clause saying nothing is lost; filed as defect #7 with `retranslate:[ar,ms]`, **not edited unilaterally** because it sits on a conversion surface. CR120's own line says what is true: *"Your Journal shows the last 30 days — 47 of these 57 are older. Nothing is deleted; they stay here."* Hence: the cap is a **view default with an in-place escape hatch, never a fetch limit** (`SHOW ALL 57` reads the Portfolio's own durable data), and the Journal pointer is **plan-aware** — *"Journal keeps 30 days on Floor Pass — 47 of these 57 are older. They stay here."* **The cap, decided by Saiful: last 25, with the span they cover stated** (`LAST 25 CLOSED · 17 MAY – 28 JUL`) — the period is **described, never used to filter**, because a pure period filter shows an empty history to a user who took a break and shows all 200 to a day-trader who did not, while a combination must choose union (unbounded) or intersection (empty). Above it sits a summary computed over **all** closed trades, not the visible 25 (a hit rate over an arbitrary display window is a wrong number wearing the authority of a statistic): win/loss bar, `WON 41 · LOST 16 · 72% · NET +$39,330`. **Four structures built and measured on identical data before the call** — landing screens at modest / six-month / heavy, plus the worst state a user can reach: **today 3.6 / 8.9 / 25.4** (no other state exists); **bounded dashboard 2.5 / 3.0 / 3.2** (3.2, bounded by construction); **segmented tabs 1.0 / 1.4 / 2.3** as first built, before open trades moved to the landing tab; **collapsible sections 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.4** (**9.7 with everything expanded** — a number the user can undo with two taps). I recommended the bounded dashboard and flagged the tab risk — a horizontal switcher nested inside the bottom-nav tab the user is already in, with **no tab pattern anywhere in the app** outside `alpaca_connect_screen.dart`. Saiful chose tabs; the mitigations are below. **STRUCTURE DECIDED 2026-07-29 — segmented tabs.** Saiful chose tabs after reviewing all four in the prototype. Three hex-clipped segments (`cornerCut: 8`, matching `ticker_chart.dart:185` and CR106's BOARD|TRANSCRIPT toggle) under a pinned compact value card; fill flip only, no sliding indicator and **no swipe-between-tabs** (the DS rules out motion on text, and a horizontal swipe inside a bottom-nav tab fights the OS back gesture). **POSITIONS carries holdings AND open trades, so HISTORY is closed trades only and its count says `195`, not `200`** — this is the one thing the structure could get wrong, since an open trade is money at risk with a stop that can fire and a tab the user does not land on makes it invisible; it also dissolves the interleave defect, because no list contains both any more. The sector donut moves inside Positions where it describes the list beneath it. **Tab state is `TabController` state, never a persisted preference.** Saiful asked whether the Portfolio should land on Positions or resume the last tab; the answer is *both, at different scopes*, and the shipped shell already gives all three for free — `home_shell.dart:42` hosts the nav destinations in an **`IndexedStack`**, so `PortfolioScreen`'s State lives for the whole app session: a push-and-pop keeps the tab, a bottom-nav round trip keeps the tab, and a relaunch lands on Positions. **Doing nothing is the whole implementation** — no prefs key, no stale-preference migration, none of CR106's T-MODESIDE trap surface. Persisting across launches is rejected for the same reason open trades moved onto the landing tab: a user whose last visit ended on History would open the app the next day with an armed stop behind a tab they cannot see, and since the pinned value card shows total value, P&L and cash on every tab regardless, the *only* thing landing on History costs is sight of the live positions. A staleness rule ("reset if resumed after N minutes") is also rejected — a tab that sometimes remembers and sometimes does not is worse than either rule applied consistently. **The Positions tab carries a live pip when an open trade exists**, since its count is holdings and therefore under-reports its own contents; a second number would conflate two different things and tab labels have no width to spare, so it is a 6pt flat-top hex in family cyan — **not amber, because an open position is a state, not a warning** — that turns `textHigh` when the tab is active and is absent when there are none. **A list over 12 items gets search + sort inside its own tab** (what a full viewport per list buys, and what the rejected dashboard could not offer without a navigation), with per-list defaults rather than one generic sort: holdings by value, watchlist A–Z (a watchlist is scanned to *find* a name, and movers-first moves the name every day), closed newest. **Measured per tab** — Positions 1.1 / 1.7 / 2.9, Watchlist 1.0 / 2.0 / 4.2, History 2.8 / 3.7 / 3.7 screens across modest / six-month / heavy: **History stops growing at six months**, which is the 25-cap doing its job, while **Watchlist is the one unbounded tab** and is unbounded for a reason nobody chose (the auto-add above) — search and sort make 40 rows navigable, not 200, so that needs its own conversation if the auto-add stays. The summary strip is captioned `ACROSS ALL 195 CLOSED` so it cannot be read as a statistic about the visible 25. Tab labels are the tightest strings on the screen (~117pt each); `POSITIONS 12` fits at 1.0 and 1.15 in EN, and **AR/MS need re-checking once translated** — a `FittedBox` shrinking a tab label is CR108 over again. Rejected: the bounded dashboard (flattest at 3.2 and nothing behind a mode, but no list ever gets a full viewport) and collapsible sections (2.4 screens is a state the user can undo with two taps → 9.7); both kept live in the prototype so the comparison stays auditable. **RTL verification caught a live instance of CR106's T-BIDI trap**: `+$5,423.69 (+5.33%)` reordered to `(5.33%+` — every run mixing sign, digits and parens is now bidi-isolated (the layout mirrors, the numbers do not). **Phase 1 needs nothing from the backend** — structure + section split + the 25-cap + the summary + the plan-aware pointer are all view concerns over data already fetched, plus `ListView.builder`; pagination (`limit`/`offset`/`total` on `GET /v1/sim/trades`, and honouring the existing unused `status=` filter) is Phase 3, wanted by the pushed all-trades route which today fetches the whole ledger to render a 25-row tab. **Seven defects spotted, flagged to the Architect to mint, not filed here:** open trades buried in history; the eager `ListView(children:)` itself; the trade→journal write wrapped in `except Exception: pass` (`sim.py:328` and two more — silent, and much more expensive once the Portfolio points at the Journal); the Journal list endpoint at `limit=100` with no pagination despite returning `total`; the undisclosed auto-growing watchlist; `_WatchlistRow` setting the price at 24px `statMid` against a 12px ticker, so the price shouts and the identity whispers; and **`journalRetentionWarning` claiming a data loss that does not happen** (see above — one verb, but on a paid-conversion surface). `retranslate:[ar,ms]` — 16 proposed ARB ids in the spec. Prototype: 4 structures × 3 account sizes × dark/light × LTR/RTL × 1.0/1.15 × Floor Pass/Trader, with the rendered scroll height, screen count and row count **read live from the DOM** under the phone rather than claimed. Spec: [CR120_portfolio_list_structure/](CR120_portfolio_list_structure/). **PHASE 1 BUILT, AUDITED AND INTEGRATED (2026-07-29, AT:R65).** Laned to `coder.mobile` under `GATE: independent`, built on `lane/CR120.coder.mobile` @ `1601e30b`, returned **COMPLETE round 1 with zero findings** by the track-K auditor, and merged to `main` at `72a6d804`. Re-verified on main independently of both reports: **mobile 279 green** (266 before, +13 new) and `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos` exit 0 with only the 5 pre-existing infos the lane disclosed. **The assign carried six Architect decisions, and the two that mattered most were both corrections of this row's own spec.** **D1 — the spec was STALE and would have produced a wrong shape:** it names `FlatTopHexagonClipper(cornerCut: 8)` against `ticker_chart.dart:185`, but **CR117 split that class into three and deliberately left the old name binding nothing**, so every clipper clause here was wrong. The lane was redirected to `FlatTopHexagonBarClipper(endInset: 8)`, one clip around the whole bar, with `room_view_mode_toggle.dart` as the worked example — the auditor confirmed the post-CR117 name is what shipped. **D2 — `SHOW ALL` had to ship in Phase 1, not Phase 2:** a 25-row cap with no escape hatch deletes a free user's own trade history from every surface in the app, so the cap shipped with an **in-place expansion** rather than waiting for the pushed route. **D3 — retention is three states, not `int?`:** the Portfolio never calls the journal endpoint, so `retentionDays == null` is ambiguous between *unlimited* and *not yet loaded*, and the naive non-null check renders the reassuring branch to a Floor Pass user who is in fact capped — the pointer branches on `retentionDays`/`retentionLoaded` only, never on plan name and never on a hardcoded 30. Of the seven defects this row flagged, `journalRetentionWarning` was minted **DEF155** and fixed inside this lane; the eager `ListView(children:)` and the watchlist row's loudness inversion were fixed here directly. **The ARB count in this row was wrong and the worker caught it** — it says 16 proposed ids, the spec's §7 table lists **21**. **Acceptance 11 (the sector-legend cap) is NOT delivered.** It was appended by amendment `ba0aa979` *after* the worker branched at `2f49e350`, and `claude -p` is one-shot, so the lane never saw it — verified absent by grep, and **not a finding against the builder**. It and Phases 2–3 keep this row `started`. **Saiful's ruling 2026-08-20:** the shipped in-place SHOW ALL is accepted as Phase 2 (the pushed all-trades route is superseded); Phase 3 — server-side cap/pagination on GET /v1/sim/trades — stays open and is queued for the next build batch. **Phase 3 shipped 2026-08-20 (AT:R73, aa886d3a):** opt-in limit(1..500)/offset on GET /v1/sim/trades; envelope adds always-present training-scoped total (DEF269-safe by construction — count reuses training_trade_scope, game fills proven not to inflate it) + echoed limit/offset; stable opened_at DESC, id DESC order; omitted params = byte-identical response for the shipped client (verified against api_client.dart's envelope read). 7 new tests, 4 mutations proven, DEF200 baseline zero-churn. All three phases done — closing. | done | [CR120_portfolio_list_structure/](CR120_portfolio_list_structure/) | AT:UI Designer |
| CR121 | 2026-07-29 | **Client version gate: a server-driven minimum build, with a message per raise.** Saiful: *"research how I can force an update on the app on the users phone"* → *"Create a CR for the gate. Make it such that we can send a message as well to the user when we ask them to update. Message will be added for each time we move the bar."* **Measured: no gate exists at any layer** — zero hits for `min_version`/`force_update`/`upgrade_required` across `backend/app/**/*.py` and `mobile/lib/**/*.dart`. But the plumbing is already half-built and terminates in a DB column instead of a decision: the client computes its own version (`device_user.dart:46` → `"0.1.0+57"`), ships it on bootstrap (`api_client.dart:980-992` → `schemas/auth.py:65` → `api/auth.py:119`), and the server stores it (`models.py:120,189`) — it just never acts on it. **The honest ceiling:** iOS has **no** force-update API, so "force" = the app refuses to run below the floor and hands the user a one-tap route to the store. That is the only mechanism working on both platforms and every channel we use (TestFlight, Play internal/closed, App Store, cable). **Design:** the floor is *append-only, one row per raise* (`client_release_floors`), not a mutable setting — each raise carries its own `headline`/`body_en`/`body_ar`/`body_ms`, active floor = highest `min_build`, and `active=false` retracts a bad raise without losing the history. Unauthenticated `GET /v1/client/release-floor` (sibling of `/v1/health`, `main.py:209` — must answer *before* a session exists, since a blocked client may be too old to authenticate) returns a server-decided `action: block|nag|ok` plus locale-resolved copy, so policy changes without a client release; `426 Upgrade Required` enforces server-side off a new `X-App-Version` header added at the single existing choke point (`api_client.dart:52-64`), with `/v1/health`, the floor endpoint itself and the feedback POST exempt so a stuck user can still report it. Mobile catches the 426 in a `_VersionGateInterceptor` modelled on DEF073's `_ServerErrorInterceptor` (`api_client.dart:72-89`), checks on launch **and** on foreground-resume, and raises a non-dismissible screen. Write side is `POST /v1/admin/release-floor` behind the existing `ADMIN_SECRET` bearer (`api/admin.py:54-63`) — a raise is one API call, no deploy, no container recreate, which is why it's a table and not an env var. **Floor is one integer, not a per-platform pair:** `pubspec.yaml` carries a single `version: <semver>+<build>` that `build_testflight.sh:81-99` bumps and `publish_playstore.sh --no-bump` reuses, so comparison is integer `>=` on the build number, no semver parsing. **Deliberate exception to degrade-loudly:** the gate **fails open** — a fail-closed gate turns any melehost outage into a simultaneous brick of every installed client, strictly worse than briefly serving a stale build; the failure is logged and surfaced in the admin config check, never swallowed. **Sequencing constraint:** a gate only binds builds that already contain it, so `0.1.0+57` and everything before is permanently ungateable — worth landing before the next TestFlight round so `+58` is the first gateable build. **Operational footgun guarded:** the admin write path refuses a `min_build` above the highest build ever observed in `user_devices.last_app_version` without an explicit force flag, because raising the floor above what TestFlight has approved bricks every iOS tester with nowhere to go. iOS store deep link needs a numeric App Store ID we do not have (falls back to the TestFlight join link; same provisioning dependency as DEF100/CR084), and the bundle IDs differ per platform (`ai.agenticmarketintel.amiTrade` vs `ai.agenticmarketintel.ami_trade`) so nothing may derive a store URL from one value. ~5 new ARB keys need ar/ms; the per-raise message itself is operational copy with EN fallback, not shipped content. **Out of scope:** Play In-App Updates immediate flow (Android-only polish on a tap this already covers; `inAppUpdatePriority` is Publishing-API-only and unsupported on internal app sharing), Shorebird OTA (Dart-only, own CR), and bricking the legacy base by refusing `/v1/auth/device` (documented emergency lever, not built). Spec: [CR121_client_version_gate/](CR121_client_version_gate/). | done | [CR121_client_version_gate/](CR121_client_version_gate/) | AT:R66 |
| CR122 | 2026-07-29 | **Ads monetization — `AdsService` facade + house-ad inventory + AdMob, built and tested for Beta/Prod.** Floor Pass's entire revenue model (`ads.md`, locked since the initial specs) had **zero implementation**: no ads CR existed, no ad SDK in `mobile/pubspec.yaml`, no ad code in `mobile/lib/`.
