Turnover is measured against the fixed sim starting capital rather than a time-weighted average portfolio value — an explicit approximation of the Barber–Odean definition, chosen because every sim portfolio starts at the same known figure and it therefore needs no new table; **recorded as an approximation in the code, not passed off as the literal metric**. **The honesty rules are the acceptance, and both are mutation-proven:** a thin sample (< 10 trades OR < 7 days on **either** side of the boundary) returns a refusal carrying **no figure at all** — not a zero, not an extrapolation — and forcing `_meets_threshold` to `True` turns 2 tests red; dropping the preset-marker check turns 7 red. Content: 366 the Taiwan numbers without editorial; 367 the 11.4% vs 18.5% turnover finding; 368 overconfidence + the disposition effect; 369 the tilt spiral with the cortisol/testosterone literature; 370 what skill persistence actually looks like. **Sourcing was verified against primary sources, and the verification did real work — three figures were rejected rather than written:** a search-sourced Taiwan survival curve of "80% quit within 2 years, 13% by 3, 7% by 5" that appears nowhere in the primary PDF (the paper's Kaplan-Meier figures are **44%/24%/15%** at 1/2/3 years, and those are what shipped); Coates & Herbert's widely-quoted "74% testosterone rise on a winning streak", which is discussion in the PNAS paper and not a reported result; and Locke & Mann's disposition-effect cost figure, dropped because their 2000 working paper and 2005 JFE paper give irreconcilable summaries. **AUDIT ROUND 1 = AWAITING_FIXES, 1 BLOCKER, and it caught an error I had personally cleared.** 368's "men traded 45% more and earned risk-adjusted net returns 1.4 points lower / single men 67% more and 2.3 points lower" — I flagged it as suspicious, "verified" it, and passed it. What I actually checked was a **search-engine summary of the SSRN working-paper abstract**; the lesson cites the **published QJE 116(1), 2001**. The auditor fetched that PDF and read §III.A/§III.B/Table IV directly: **`2.3` appears nowhere in the cited paper**, `1.4` is real but is the *singles* figure (footnote 21's three-factor model, per a second independent pass) not the full-sample one, and — worse than the magnitude — the paper states raw net-return differences between men and women are **not statistically significant** (16.3% vs 16.9%, reversed in sign), so "men earned lower returns" was wrong in *direction*. Quiz 1 graded the wrong pairing as correct. **Round 2 fix:** the lesson now uses the cited version's own trading-cost measure end to end — 2.65pp/yr men vs 1.72 women → a **0.93pp** gap, widening to **1.44pp** among singles — so both halves come from one measure and both are quotable from the paper's own abstract. Keeping `1.4` was rejected deliberately: there is no published three-factor singles breakdown, so it would have forced mixing measures across one sentence, which is the error that caused the bug. Body, hypothesis sentence and Quiz 1 updated together. **Guard:** 368's `sources:` now carries an explicit do-not-use note naming the 1.4/2.3 pair as the superseded working-paper abstract's, because the second audit pass measured **WebSearch echoing that wrong pairing verbatim across two independent queries with no citation** — a search engine repeating a figure is not corroboration, it is the same uncited claim twice, and no test can catch that class. **MINOR also fixed:** 369 said institutions "showed no such pattern" on the break-even effect; proprietary futures firms **do** show it, they just don't move volatility/liquidity the way individuals do — the difference is market impact, not immunity. **23 of 24 numeric claims CONFIRMED** against primary sources by the auditor, several to the exact digit. Original review note retained: 368's figures  "men traded 45% more and earned risk-adjusted net returns 1.4 points lower / single men 67% more and 2.3 points lower" looked transposed against the QJE abstract's 2.65-vs-1.72 framing, but those are two different quantities in the same paper (reduction-from-trading vs the risk-adjusted net-return gap) and the working-paper abstract states 1.4 / 2.3 verbatim. 366 is careful to separate the **18.6% one-year** bar (luck included) from the **<1% persistence** bar (ranked, re-tested out of sample) and its quizzes teach that distinction, since conflating them is how one good year becomes "an edge". **No lessons manifest exists** — the catalogue is globbed at runtime by `lessons_service.py`, and `curriculum_map.md` is a stale planning doc that already stopped at 292, so nothing needed registering. The mandate leaves Settings because it is a *training instrument the curriculum tells users to revisit*, not configuration; it keeps its in-context deep links from Portfolio and Lessons. INSIGHTS is the one genuinely new surface — what your decisions look like in aggregate; rejected alternatives were credits/membership (billing — behind the gear), agents-unlocked (the Floor's whole job) and streaks (Amendment A deletes them). **§4.1 exists because the first draft overclaimed and the schema check caught it: two of the five panels are NOT computable, and are recorded rather than quietly rendered as zeros.** **§4.1 now specifies five cards, each rendered full-size in the prototype's §07 build reference with its query, source line, empty state and edge case** — the reference renders the *same* component the phone does, so spec and screen cannot drift (DEF098). All five need no new table and no migration: **how your trades ended** (`SIM_TRADE` where `'closed' in tags`, bucketed on `won`/`lost`/`manual` — `sim.py:395,448`), **what PM decided** (`ROOM_RUN` grouped by `payload.verdict.action` over APPROVE/MODIFY/REJECT/PASS/NO_VERDICT — `room_runner.py:1610`), **analysts you sought out** (`ONE_ON_ONE`/`AGENT_COACH`/`AGENT_UNLOCK`, `agents_involved[0]`), **how your mandate has moved** (`MANDATE_EDIT` diffing `payload.before` vs `payload.after` — `mandate.py:147,259`), and **daily challenge by type** (`DAILY_CHALLENGE` grouped by `payload.type` — `daily_challenge.py:223`). Two findings changed the design: **"how your trades ended" is the strongest card and the cheapest** — a user who closes by hand before stop or target is overriding the plan they wrote, which is a habit and habits are what the product exists to change, and the tags already distinguish it; and **`MANDATE_EDIT` stores full before/after mandate snapshots**, so every limit's trajectory — including whether one loosened right after a loss — is reconstructable with no new table. Caveats that stop this being a conclusion the other way: n=18 convenes cannot separate "fixed" from "rare", and the one rate that never had a guard (CR037/CR038 unhedged assertions) is still unmeasured — so the model arm is NOT justified by the historical table and waits on Phases 3–4. | CR144 | 2026-08-08 | process | **Before a pattern reads agent prose, name the field it could have read instead.** DEF231 took six audit rounds and one live defect (DEF234, `$1,073.46` parsed as `$1.00` and rendered "107900.0% ABOVE $1.00") to close a check that compares two numbers — and its own filing row had specified the right design in the sentence that justified filing it: the level is *"already a structured number the verdict carries… so a comparison is available without parsing free text"*. A general prose parser was built instead, and **all four of its defects were figures that were not levels of the run at all**. Same shape one function over: **DEF235**, where `\bsize\b` followed by any number in a 15-char gap matched *"a MEDIUM size entry at $188.62"* and AMI published a drawdown contribution **63× too large** under the words "These are the figures of record". And **CR106 B1** is the same lesson learned once already and not generalised (level provenance moved out of prose into a typed field). Nothing required anyone to ask the question, so this CR adds the rule: any regex or parser reading a value or claim out of LLM-authored text carries a comment at its definition site naming **the structured field considered instead and why it lost** — and if none exists, says whether making one is cheaper than the parser. Deliberately a comment, not a lint rule: the failure is never that someone wrote a pattern, it is that nobody asked, and a mechanical check would be satisfied mechanically while a comment is reviewable ("is that really why it lost?"). **The law behind it, now P16 Amendment 1:** a prose pattern's false-positive surface is proportional to how much **wider than the structured answer** it is, so build the structured half first and let the prose half cover only the residual — usually grammar, which no field can supply. Measured, so the trade is not theoretical: narrowing DEF231 to the run's own levels and spending the safety it bought on recall (an offline LLM sweep that found three whole verb families) took the corpus from **121 figures extracted** to **365 extracted, 246–277 matched to a structured level and actually checked**. Narrowing did not cost coverage — it is what made tripling it affordable. **P16 Amendment 2: never select the guard's corpus with the thing it guards.** The P16 fixture selected rows carrying a `$` AND a directional verb stem, making its own population a function of the pattern under test; a broadening moved the count for two reasons at once, and a **narrowing** would have shrunk the population in lockstep and hidden its own coverage loss — the one failure that fixture exists to prevent. Now `$` alone, 811 rows. **P16 Amendment 3:** two more measurement-harness bugs (`auto_adjust=False` against an app using yfinance's default; the 52-week range omitted, understating retention by 26 points), both caught by the *shape* of the unmatched list rather than by any number looking wrong. Both live prose patterns brought into compliance: `_DIRECTIONAL_CLAIMS` states its division of labour, and `_LEVEL_PATTERNS` carries the question **as a question** — DEF235 is open and owned by the CR143 track, so this CR records what must be asked and explicitly does not pre-empt the fix. Docs + comments only; no behaviour change. | done | `docs/forward_planning/CR144_prose_pattern_field_first/` | AT:R66 |

Gross debt renders beside the netted figure because a netted number hides leverage — $40B cash against $45B debt and $1B against $6B both render as *net debt $5,000M*, and those are not the same balance sheet. (2) One nullable `prompt_version` column on `llm_audit`, written by the gateway alongside `system_prompt`. Nullable and additive — old rows stay NULL, which honestly means "unversioned", not "version zero" (CR040). | CR163 | 2026-08-10 | **An autonomous bug crawler on the simulator — find defects nobody thought to write a test for, and feed them to the fixer/auditor pipeline.** Saiful, 2026-08-10: *"since we are running lean, I want to be able to use the simulations to work out bugs so they can be fixed. I need you to create a framework where we can do this autonomously."* The existing harness (CR080, CR162) only finds bugs someone already imagined — every check is an assertion a human wrote about a screen a human listed — which does not scale for a one-person team and structurally cannot find the surprising defects, which are the expensive ones. **CR162 made the alternative possible:** once the accessibility semantics tree is exposed the app is *enumerable*, so the harness can list every addressable control and explore on its own; coverage then grows by walking further rather than by writing more tests. Three separated parts: **explorer** (`crawler/explorer.py`, breadth-first walk under a wall-clock budget), **oracles** (`crawler/oracles.py` + `crawler/errorsink.py` — anything that can call a screen wrong with no screen-specific assertion: Flutter framework errors, layout overflow, controls under the safe area, sparse screens, unlabelled controls), and **ledger + triage** (`crawler/ledger.py`, `tools/triage.py` — fingerprint, suppress what is already triaged, promote the rest). Entry point `scripts/crawl_ios_sim.sh`. **The finding that redirected the design, measured rather than assumed:** the first implementation read Flutter's errors from the device log, and that does not work — a `simctl spawn log stream` capture of a live `Runner` process, taken while the app was actively calling `debugPrint`, returned **5,685 lines and zero Dart-origin entries**; every apparent "flutter" match was a CFBundle resource lookup. Dart stdout/stderr goes to the process's own stdout, which `os_log` never sees (`flutter run` shows those lines only because it holds the pipe). So the app records its own errors instead — `mobile/lib/qa/error_sink.dart` installs `FlutterError.onError` + `PlatformDispatcher.onError` behind CR162's existing `--dart-define=AMI_QA_SEMANTICS=1` and appends de-duplicated JSONL to the app container, which the crawler reads back via `simctl get_app_container`; uniform across platforms, survives the crawler crashing, no new transport. **Debug build by Saiful's call** — Flutter compiles most framework assertions out of release, so a release crawl finds only hard crashes; the trade is that timing-sensitive findings are leads, not measurements. **The crawler deliberately files nothing.** CR080 twice had a harness bug written up as application failures, the worst being one `TypeError` reported as 27 failing tests, none real — and Saiful's pipeline puts a **fixer agent waiting on whatever is filed**, so an auto-filing crawler plus an auto-fixing agent turns one bad build into a branch full of fixes for defects that never existed. `tools/triage.py` is the gate; it writes **intake stubs**, not `DEF###` rows, because ids are minted by a single owner to avoid collisions and a script minting them autonomously is exactly that race. From the stub the existing machinery takes over: Architect mints + writes the assign lane → `coder.*` fixes → auditor verdict (`DISPATCH_PROTOCOL.md`). **Decisions not to re-litigate:** the frontier holds *replayable paths*, not screen fingerprints (the first version queued fingerprints, which is unimplementable — there is no `goto(fingerprint)` — so depth > 1 silently never worked); the budget is wall-clock, not step count (steps range 200ms–seconds, so a step budget makes runs incomparable); destructive controls are never tapped, and the deny-list is asserted in `tests_offline/` rather than trusted, because this drives the real Alpha backend with a real account; the scroll oracle runs LAST because it swipes, and the explorer re-reads controls afterwards rather than tapping nodes enumerated before the screen moved; a missing error sink is a hard failure and never "no errors found"; and seen ≠ triaged, so a merely-reported finding keeps being reported until an explicit `filed`/`false_positive`/`wontfix` decision silences it. **Out of scope:** scheduling (Saiful chose "on-demand now, scheduled once it's proven"), Android (the design is platform-neutral — the sink is a file on both — but only the iOS simulator path is built here), and auto-fixing (the fixer + auditor already exist in `orchestration/dispatch/`; this feeds them). Binding design rule from plan review: **same infrastructure as the main app** — no forked data layer or Room path, so any infra change is re-testable by re-running the harness. Locked decisions: outcome edge primary (1w/4w forward returns, APPROVE vs PASS vs random-pick vs SPY); staged ~130-convene pilot → ~800–1000 full; news ablated in v1 (schema reserves `news_archive` for an Alpha-Vantage/GDELT arm); social ablated (no historical endpoint; CR035 arm-C precedent); **EDGAR companyfacts PIT fundamentals in v1** (filed-date-keyed, leakage-correct). What it builds: (1) `AsOfContext` threaded per-run via ContextVar — request-scoped, never env-flipped (reversal of CR035's arm mechanism that degraded live Alpha); (2) `price_history_daily` extended to OHLCV with `as_of` cutoff reads — one price store for Room, Portfolio Health, and scoring; (3) `fetch_fundamentals(ticker, as_of=None)` — one module, live yfinance path vs EDGAR PIT path, identical dict shape; non-reconstructable fields (forward P/E, PEG, analyst target/rating, next earnings) flow to the existing `field_state = UNAVAILABLE` machinery (CR104/DEF123), structurally not prompt-instructed; (4) admin-only `POST /v1/admin/backtest/room-run` (public `RoomStartRequest` never grows the field); (5) sweep driver factored from `room_benchmark.py`, resumable, run inside the alpha container; (6) scoring from the snapshot store only (byte-reproducible), date-clustered inference (effective n ≈ #as-of dates), per-date random-pick bootstrap null, target/stop-hit gated on `level_provenance`; (7) structural leakage guards: store-level `AsOfLeakageError`, post-run `llm_audit` prompt scan, model-cutoff probe fixing `window_start = collapse-month + 8w` (both benchmark lanes — `docs/benchmark/claude/`, `kimi/` — hold pre-cutoff LLM backtests invalid on their face; only ~late-2025→mid-2026 is scoreable). Survivorship: `tickers_150` reused with a written membership audit (`backtest_universe_membership`), counts published verbatim. Payoff beyond the one-off result: a pinned regression batch (same spec, new batch_id) makes "infra changed → re-test the Room" a routine ~1.5 h operation. Limitations register ships with the report (no Sharpe — no SELL/portfolio; ~12% verdict-flip noise floor; tested Room ≠ live Room under ablations). Related: CR035 (the harness lineage), CR136 (`price_history_daily`), CR157 (weekly retrospective of live runs — distinct, stays proposed), CR158 (`prompt_version` epochs). Plan: approved 2026-08-10 in-session. **DONE 2026-08-22 (AT:R74) — all five acceptance criteria, checked against the spec rather than the prose.** **(1)** 46 unit tests green at HEAD across `test_cr164_asof_backtest.py` + `test_cr164_pit_field_coverage.py` — leakage raise on seeded post-as_of rows, UNAVAILABLE rendering of ablated fields, `run_date` anchored at the as-of date, and the live path provably unchanged when no context is active. **(2)** Pilot gate passed at `pit-pilot-2`. **(3)** The full sweep completed: `r70-outcome-2`, 450 planned / 446 scored / 18 as-of dates, with tranche-wise prompt scans, and the report is byte-reproducible by contract (every RNG seeded, every iteration sorted, report date pinned by `--stamp`). **(4)** `results/report_r70-outcome-2.md` ships the 7-item limitations register inline — no Sharpe, the ~12% verdict-flip noise floor, tested-Room ≠ live-Room, effective n = **18 dates not 446 runs**, the pre-cutoff exclusion, the survivorship audit counts, and the execution assumptions. **(5) was the only real gap and is now closed**: [`RETEST_RECIPE.md`](CR164_room_backtest/RETEST_RECIPE.md) documents the pinned batch as the post-infra-CR re-test operation — the plan file with its SHA-256 pinned and verified byte-identical between the repo and melehost (`cf4974b4…`), why `--pairs-file` and never `--seed` alone (seed-plus-window reproduces a plan only if `--window-end` is pinned too; omit it and the Friday count shifts with the calendar and silently changes pairs), the supervisor invocation, the two exit codes that mean stop rather than retry (DEF336's outage abort, DEF345's missing sentinel), and the baseline table to diff against. The recipe that existed before this was the **pilot-era** one in `FINDINGS_2026-08-11.md` §7 (`--n-pairs 26 --repeat-pairs 0`), written before Phase A and Phase B ran and describing a batch nobody would replay today. **The recipe states its own limit, deliberately:** the block-bootstrap CI spans zero (−2.05%..+4.43% on a +1.15% APPROVE−PASS spread, pooled null p=0.3010), so a re-test is a **regression check against a quantified noise floor, not a promotion gate** — it must never be reported as evidence a change improved the Room. **DEF358 found and fixed while writing it:** the completion sentinel counted the process rather than the batch, so `r70-outcome-2` — which finished all 450 pairs across supervisor relaunches — stamped `completed: 50` and the report printed that verbatim under a **COMPLETE** label, one line above `Index rows: 450`. Nothing was mis-scored; the trust signal was. | done | [CR164_room_backtest/](CR164_room_backtest/) | AT:R67 |
| CR165 | 2026-08-11 | **A dispassionate catalogue of the 50 largest US/English YouTube channels that claim to teach investing — URL, strategy class, monetisation, and what each sells.** Saiful, 2026-08-11: *"research the popolar internet and youtube channels that are now suggesting that they can teach you investing… this research is dispasionate. do not editorialized. that would be my job later on."* Scope answered by him: **US/English only**, YouTube as entry point **plus** the paid product it funnels to, **50 entries ranked by popularity**, tiered **15 full-detail / 15 four-to-eight lines / 20 two-to-three lines**. **The constraint that shaped the work is the no-editorializing one**, because a survey of this field invites judgement at every line: every entry is evidenced from the channel's **own About text and a sample of its most recent upload titles** (read from each channel's own YouTube page with `hl=en&gl=US`, 2026-08-11 — no count taken from a listicle); creator claims are quoted and attributed, never asserted and never rebutted in line; the **only ordering is subscriber count**, with no quality ranking anywhere; evaluative vocabulary is absent by construction and grep-verified; and **regulatory facts appear only with a primary source** (FTC/SEC/court by URL) — exactly one entry qualified, Warrior Trading's April 2022 FTC action ($3M, and $2.9M returned to 20,402 people in Jan 2023) — with absence documented as "nothing located", never as a clean record. Method: ~95 candidates from two independent seeds (published roundups, which over-index on passive/personal-finance creators, **and** YouTube channel-search per strategy term, the only way the trading-education half of the field surfaces at all), verified, screened by a stated inclusion rule, ranked, tiered. **Findings worth flagging, as facts:** popularity rank and strategy coverage pull in opposite directions — the 510K cut line removes almost the entire options, value, dividend and retirement-decumulation segments (tastylive, projectoption, Motley Fool, Timothy Sykes, Everything Money, Option Alpha, IBD and ~35 more sit below rank 50), so **Appendix A** lists them by strategy class rather than hiding the effect; two of the top 50 monetise the audience with **nothing** (Aswath Damodaran, Two Cents/PBS); two funnel to a **security** rather than education (Cardone Capital's funds, the Meet Kevin Pricing Power ETF); three large personal-finance-branded channels publish **no investing instruction in recent output** (Caleb Hammer, Erika Kullberg, Charlie Chang) and are kept at rank with an `adjacent` label and the evidence quoted rather than silently dropped; and vendor pricing is often unobtainable (warriortrading.com returns HTTP 403 to direct fetch), recorded as unverified rather than estimated. **Nothing was dropped silently** — **Appendix B** lists every screened-out channel with the rule that removed it (Valuetainment/Codie Sanchez = business, Karlton Dennis/Mark Kohler = tax, NickRTFM = EA FC Ultimate Team not securities, plus the non-US set: Coin Bureau, Rayner Teo, Ben Felix, Patrick Boyle et al). **Out of scope:** AR/MS creators (offered and declined for this pass), non-YouTube-first surfaces, audience-overlap or revenue estimation, and any assessment of teaching quality — Saiful does that pass. | CR166 | 2026-08-11 | quality | **Census the data we already hold, before adding one more field by hand.** Saiful, 2026-08-11: *"look at what else we can give the agents to help with the decisions. how do we determine what else the agents need? remember we do not let the agent calculate. all numbers should be provided."* Out of a live AAPL convene benchmarked against an external TradingAgents report for the same ticker/date, then a supply-side audit of `fundamentals.py` / `technicals.py` / `market_data.py` / `room_prompts.py`. **The pattern nobody has named:** missing fact-sheet fields are being discovered one at a time, per agent, each costing a full review cycle — CR145 Tier A found `marketCap`/`freeCashflow`/`totalDebt` *"already fetched then discarded"*, CR150 found beta/volatility/short-interest by reviewing the Bear, CR152 found five compliance inputs *"promised and never rendered, all already computed"* by reviewing the Trader. Each correct; together, the same root cause rediscovered three times with nobody looking at the whole supply. Market cap is the proof — *"Avoid microcaps (< $500M market cap)"* was a HARD constraint in 17/18 prompts against 0/18 sheets stating one, and it sat unfollowable for months because the field was never *missing*, it was fetched and thrown away. **So the census was run (2026-08-11, live yfinance): the single `yf.Ticker(t).info` call we already make returns 180 keys, 132 of them numeric; we read 23; 112 numeric fields are already in memory and never passed to any agent.** Zero additional calls, no cache needed — CR145 Tier D is blocked on a fundamentals cache because it proposes *extra* calls (`.income_stmt`/`.cashflow`); this proposes none. Availability verified across AAPL/PLTR/RIVN/SNDK (mega-cap, grower, loss-maker, mid-cap): 29–33 of 33 candidate fields present, every absence semantically meaningful and already handled by CR104 `field_state`. **The prompts are being corrected against the wrong side of the mismatch:** `fundamentals_analyst.md` says *"no gross margin … is computed, so do not describe either"* while `grossMargins` (0.48653), `operatingMargins` (0.32623) and `ebitdaMargins` sit in the dict we already fetch; CR145 Batch 6 resolved that mismatch by **deleting the demand**, which against a held field is the wrong direction — and is exactly the failure mode a census prevents, since without an inventory a prompt/data mismatch looks like an over-ambitious prompt every time, never an under-served one. (The *trend* half of that sentence stays correct and stays in CR145 Tier D.) **Method — Saiful's constraint is the instrument.** If agents never calculate, every number an agent states must already be on its sheet, so the gap is a measurable residual, not a judgement: **Need = numbers agents state − numbers we gave them.** `prompt_quality_sweep.py` M3 already computes it (grounded / inherited / **novel**); novel IS the residual and M3 stops at counting it. Three legs: **(1)** triage novel into derivable → *precompute and hand over* (required by the no-calculation rule; carries a free correctness check that already has a fourth DEF066-class hit in hand), sourceable → render, unsourceable → forbid explicitly (CR038/DEF053), out-of-lane → CR145's firewall regression metric; **(2)** the unfollowable-constraint audit — static, cheap, run first, the method that found market cap and CR152's five, never yet run across all rules; **(3)** the job-description audit, judged, last, because **Leg 1 is a lagging indicator** — it measures demand for numbers agents think to reach for, and an agent never given a 200-day SMA does not say *"200-day unavailable"*, it simply never discusses the primary trend. **Scope. A:** the census script itself in CI, failing when a fetched field reaches no agent in either direction — the durable deliverable, one layer earlier than `test_prompt_data_parity.py`. **B:** fields already fetched and never passed, each binding to a named rule or role line **and a lane** — fundamentals: `trailingEps` (we render a P/E on two bases with no earnings behind either), `totalRevenue`/`revenuePerShare` (growth % with no base), the margin structure, `returnOnEquity`/`returnOnAssets`/`currentRatio`/`quickRatio`/`debtToEquity` (*"balance sheet strength"* served today by two debt figures and nothing on returns), `payoutRatio` + `trailingAnnualDividendRate` + `dividendDate` (*"capital allocation"*; `ex_dividend_date`/`dividend_rate` are **already on the `EarningsInfo` object the Room renders the earnings line from** — CR030 — and dropped at the render site), and the analyst dispersion (`numberOfAnalystOpinions`, target high/low/median, `recommendationMean` — we render *"buy, target $322.28"* and hide that 41 analysts back it across 215–400); technicals: **`twoHundredDayAverage`** (**zero hits for "200-day" anywhere in either register** — no agent can discuss the primary trend, and `compute_technicals` *cannot* compute one since `_HISTORY_PERIOD = "3m"` ≈ 65 bars, but the value is in the dict already fetched), `previousClose` + `regularMarketChangePercent` (the sheet states a price and never says whether it moved; `Quote` already carries `change_pct` and `market_state` and grep finds **zero** references to either in `room_prompts.py`/`room_runner.py`), `52WeekChange` + `SandP52WeekChange` (relative strength vs the index, free), volume absolutes, and `fiftyDayAverage` as a free cross-check against our own (a divergence is a data-quality signal, the shape `_reference_price_line` already reconciles for price). **C:** derived figures agents still assemble — % distance to the 20-day SMA and the 50-day range **high** (we do target, range low, both 52-week ends and the 50-day SMA, but not the two an agent reaches for to argue upside), and position size in shares/dollars at the mandate cap (`trading_math/portfolio.py` already converts size%→qty). **D:** a defect needing its own ID — `aggressive_debator` stated *"0.30 pt drawdown contribution from a 3.0% position with a 6.0% stop"* on the AAPL run of 2026-08-11 10:46 UTC where the correct figure is **0.18 pt**, supplied in its own prompt and quoted correctly by the Conservative and Neutral; this is DEF066's class a **fourth** time and it **slips DEF241's guard**, since the *"AMI computed this"* line is appended only when the agent's size differs from the reference ceiling (`abs(agent_size_pct - size) > 0.01`, `room_prompts.py:411`) and the Aggressive argues *at* the ceiling. **Explicitly NOT in scope, checked against the register rather than assumed — several fields that would otherwise have been proposed are already claimed, and re-proposing them would have been the exact per-agent rediscovery this CR is filed against:** ATR/realised vol (CR152 + CR150, and **explicitly REJECTED for the Market Analyst by CR146** — *"ATR keeps its merit as a stop-distance input for the Trader, a different CR"*), beta and short interest (CR150, with its *"reported-as-of, not live"* labelling requirement), margin *trend* and buybacks (CR145 Tier D, correctly blocked on the cache), raw OHLCV in the prompt (rejected by CR146 on budget, and it would hand agents a series to compute from — precisely what the no-calculation rule forbids), revenue segments / M&A / guidance (CR145's out-of-scope, need a provider); **rejected outright:** governance risk scores (`auditRisk`/`boardRisk`/`overallRisk` — opaque proprietary scores with no published methodology, we would lend our credibility to a number we cannot explain), `allTimeLow` (split-adjusted to $0.049 for AAPL — arithmetically true, analytically meaningless, and a base an agent could build a *"99.98% above the low"* claim on), and bid/ask/epoch plumbing. **The argument against this CR, stated because it is the central design question:** it pushes directly against CR145 Tier C, which shipped 2026-08-11 and made sheets **smaller** (fundamentals −30.5%, market −53.9%, news −53.0%, social −54.8%). Three conditions of shipping, not mitigations: lane assignment is mandatory per field (CR145 removed *other desks'* data, not depth — adding depth *within* a lane is the complementary move); every field names the rule it serves or is rejected (the rejected list is that discipline applied, not described); and net against deletions (the Market Analyst lost 53.9% and can afford a primary-trend line; full-sheet agents cannot afford all of Tier B and should take Tier C first). **Honest weakness:** the census measures **supply, not demand** — 112 unused fields is a fact about our code, not evidence any agent needs them. Leg 1's residual is the demand measurement and **it has not been run**: the prompt epoch changed 2026-08-11 12:54 UTC (`19cb0e3c`) so no valid corpus exists, and `prompt_quality_sweep.py` refuses pooling across a prompt change. **Tier B is a ranked hypothesis set, not a proven roster.** Second-order risk: more numbers is not more reasoning — the AAPL run put twelve agents on ~six shared figures and the failure was information *diversity*; a wider sheet could as easily yield twelve agents reciting sixty. **Acceptance:** census script in CI failing in both directions; per-field `field_state` (CR104), absent-not-labelled when not live (DEF053), rendered on both surfaces so Room and 1-on-1 cannot disagree; **and the gate that matters — a post-promotion Leg 1 re-measure on ≥30 convenes against a same-epoch baseline, where novel SHOULD fall; if it does not, the fields were not the constraint and Tier B is partially reverted rather than extended** (a change whose effect is not re-measured is the CR105 Amendment-1 trap). **NOT claimed on merge:** that any agent *uses* a new field, that reasoning improved, or that the residual closed — all response-side, all needing the corpus that does not yet exist. **Open for Saiful:** (1) does Tier B ship at all given CR145 Tier C just halved the sheets — same shape of decision as the default-open/firewall call he took for Tier C; recommend yes, lane-assigned and staged, technicals first; (2) run Leg 1 before or after Tier B — recommend **before** (~40 convenes, ~2 h, ~480 credits, frozen epoch), it is the only thing converting this from a well-argued list into a determination; (3) gross margin — supply the field or keep CR145 Batch 6's deletion; one of the two should change. **CR168 FOLDED IN HERE, 2026-08-12.** CR168 (resolved instrument identity) was the *string* half of this same dict and is now `dropped` as a standalone item — not because it was wrong, but because keeping it separate rebuilds the per-field rediscovery this census exists to stop. **It arrives with its gate already run and its own premise corrected**, so it costs this CR evidence-gathering rather than adding it: 0 wrong-company instances in 216 real turns (95% upper bound 1.4%), so it is prophylactic, not a correctness fix. **But the supply is real and unreliable** — a company *name* reaches the model in **156/216 = 72.2%** of production prompts, entirely via the `Catalysts —` news-headline line and never as identity, dropping to **66.7%** after Batch 9's 7-day recency floor, and reaching **0%** for **AMD, AVGO and KTOS**. Supply tracks news recency, not ticker-guessability: the floor removed SNOA's entire supply (its only name-bearing headlines were 353 and 358 days old), i.e. the least-guessable ticker in the set. In the AAPL corpus the prompt names **Nvidia, Amazon and OpenAI** and never Apple. **Three amendments ride along:** (a) `longName` + `exchange` are already in memory at `fundamentals.py:163` — zero additional network calls, the same constraint this CR works under; (b) `exchange` returns **codes** (`NMS`/`NYQ`/`NCM`), not names — map them or drop the field, since `Exchange: NMS` is jargon to the model; (c) Batch 5 made `_format_profile(profile, agent_id)` and DEF268 pins `_EXPECTED_LANES` literally, so any new field needs an explicit lane assignment rather than rendering to all twelve. **Free acceptance fixture:** `NBIS` resolves (`exchange: NMS`) with **`longName: null`** — a genuine half-populated identity, better than an unrecognised ticker. The technicals lane now has the lowest measurable marginal return; the rising, measured demand is in **fundamentals**, and the memo's own second reading explains why, since Batch 5 firewalled `fundamentals_analyst` **out of** technicals/news/social and may have starved it in its own lane. **This does not retire the 200-day argument:** Leg 3 exists because Leg 1 is a lagging indicator — an agent never given a 200-day SMA does not write *"200-day unavailable"*, it simply never discusses the primary trend, so 0.6% novel is blindness on that field, not sufficiency. Technicals moves later on **relative** return, not because the hole closed. **DECISIONS TAKEN (Saiful, 2026-08-13):** (1) Tier B ships staged and lane-assigned, **`fundamentals` lane FIRST** — revised from technicals on the evidence above; (2) Leg 1 before Tier B — **satisfied**, no new run commissioned; (3) gross margin — **supply the field and restore the ask** (`grossMargins`/`operatingMargins`/`ebitdaMargins` render and the margin-structure line returns to `fundamentals_analyst.md`; the margin *trend* half of the disclosure stays correct and stays in CR145 Tier D); (4) **Tier D stays inside CR166** — no separate DEF ID for the `aggressive_debator` 0.30-vs-0.18 recurrence. **STAGE 1 SCOPE** (first promotion): Tier A census guard + Tier B fundamentals lane + decision 3 + Tier D + **the folded CR168 identity fields**. Identity rides Stage 1 because it is the same dict, the same fetcher and the same renderer, and because it is **string-only** — M3 counts numeric tokens, so identity cannot move the novel rate and cannot confound this stage's gate. | CR167 | 2026-08-11 | **What the repo we forked from learned in the 106 commits since our snapshot — and the second clone that keeps the question cheap to ask again.** Saiful, 2026-08-11: *"we owe our DNA to the trading agent repo on github. lets have a look if they have made any changes specially to the agent prompts"*, then *"memo, file, no build. I want to be able to study the differences"* and *"keep our snapshot as a basis of where we fork from. if needed, can we make a second copy that will track the head?"*. **Two mounts now:** `/Volumes/Extreme Pro/TradingAgent/` stays frozen at `7e9e7b8` (2026-05-01) as the fork-basis record, never fetched; `/Volumes/Extreme Pro/TradingAgent_upstream/` is a fresh clone tracking `main`, at `a33fd4c` (2026-07-18). `7e9e7b8` is an ancestor of upstream `main`, so the clone alone produces every fork-basis→HEAD diff and the frozen copy is never touched. **106 commits** (measured by `rev-list --count`, not the compare API's summary), two releases, **21 touching `tradingagents/agents/`**. We are not downstream of their code — `backend/pyproject.toml:39` has the install commented out and our prompts are ours (CR143 Phase 1 measured `content/agents/*.md` at 10–18% of the assembled prompt) — so this is idea drift, not a merge. **They hit two of our own failure classes independently:** (a) their `social_media_analyst` prompt demanded social analysis with only a Yahoo news tool behind it and models *"fabricate Reddit/X/StockTwits content under prompt pressure (verified live)"* — our DEF063/CR024, and their fix is the pre-fetch-into-the-prompt shape we already run, plus a structured sentiment header (`e80636f`) and then `7aef10a` paying back the substance that constraining the field cost; (b) `47cbb32` shipped a market-analyst clause ordering a `get_verified_market_snapshot` call and `4e7821d` registered the tool in the ToolNode **fourteen days later**, the model meanwhile reporting it *"unavailable"* and silently skipping verification — the CR040 degrade-loudly class (DEF038/DEF063/DEF082/DEF084) occurring upstream, on the very feature meant to stop fabrication, and fixed with an executor-registration regression guard of the same shape as our `test_config_compose_parity.py`. **Two things they have that we do not**, both filed rather than built: resolved instrument identity (**CR168**) and the as-of date at the head of the prompt (**CR169**). **Where we are ahead, recorded so a later session does not re-open it as an obvious win:** their number-grounding is a tool the model may elect to call, ours is a fact sheet under a line-1 GROUNDING DIRECTIVE it cannot avoid reading — their own 14-day dark window is the argument against the tool form, and CR143 §4 already rejected the numeral-sweep guard on measurement (92.6% grounded / 3.1% inherited / 4.3% novel, every novel figure hand-read and legitimate). | CR171 | 2026-08-11 | **Short selling, borrow cost and forced buy-in — closes DEF262 by building what the `long_only` flag already promises.** From Saiful, reviewing CR170: *"can we do on sell as well ? and can we 'charge' a fee for 'borrowing' a ticker?"* — two questions that are one question, since stop/target on a sell only mean something if a sell can *open* a position and "borrowing a ticker" is the short borrow fee. Scope per his CR170 instruction, *"it should train the user with all the market capability."* **The switch already exists and lies:** `Compliance.long_only` is a live Settings toggle; flipping it makes the agents discuss shorts (`overlay_generator` branches ×4) and makes `brief_engine.py:161` tell the user *"Toggle long_only off in your Mandate first if you want to allow shorts"* — while `safety_floor.py:273-278` is a bare `pass  # delegated to trade service` and `_execute_fill` refuses the short unconditionally, stamped `blocked_by="long_only"`, the flag they just turned off (DEF262). Shorting is **not** in the rejected register. **Build AFTER CR170** (Saiful's call): a short entry is a sell-to-open, so it belongs in CR170's resting-order book; the other order builds that book twice. **Three decisions carry the design.** (1) **Short proceeds never enter `current_cash`** — only the 50% initial margin leaves cash, and `total_value` gains a short leg; crediting proceeds would make an unspendable credit indistinguishable from a profit in the NAV series, corrupting `total_drawdown_pct`, `portfolio_nav_daily`, TWR and `_risk_limit_context` (the CR170 reserved-cash hazard, one level worse). (2) **Separate `sim_short_positions` table, never a negative `SimHoldingRow.quantity`** — `backend/scripts/def110_backfill.py::expected()` subtracts open SELL rows to detect phantom shares and would fire on every user with a short, and `compute_lots_fifo` cannot walk negative lots. (3) **A sell never crosses zero** — `h >= q` closes (byte-identical to today), `h == 0` opens a short, `0 < h < q` is **refused**; splitting one action into a close plus a short is the P&L-attribution bug class DEF166 and DEF110 already cost us twice, and refusing it costs one sentence of copy. Loss containment is **forced buy-in at a 1.30 maintenance ratio** (Saiful, over a size cap or negative equity), market-hours gated so a margin close never fires against a stale price, executed through the existing `_execute_fill`, and **never refused for insufficient cash** — the collateral is already posted, and containment that fails when needed is not containment. Also still open: the mobile wiring that opens the already-built ticket off `verdict.strategy`/`legs`, §11's NAV/FIFO tail, and the dividend/option-marks feeds. **CRITERION 1 PROVEN (2026-08-22, AT:R73) — `test_cr172_no_behaviour_change.py`, 44 tests, 8/8 mutations killed.** The criterion is worded *"proven by test, not asserted"* and the proof had never been written: the gate existed and was mutation-proven, the byte-identity was not. **The oracle is frozen historical code** — `Portfolio.total_value`'s body copied verbatim from `git show 4c072f09^`, the commit before the option term landed. A second implementation of today's rule would be DEF098's two-renderers shape and would drift into agreeing with whatever the code does; a differential against code that cannot move is the only thing that can answer "byte-identical to before", and the file says a future change making the oracle wrong needs a CR, never a re-sync. **`repr`, not `==`** — CPython's float repr is the shortest round-tripping string, so two floats share a repr exactly when they share every bit, while `==` is wrong in both directions (it calls `0.0` and `-0.0` equal, and a NaN unequal to itself); `approx` would be wronger still, since "within a tolerance" is the claim the criterion exists to refuse. Coverage runs one clause at a time: `total_value` and drawdown over 18 parametrised cases (six books x three mark sets — a cash figure not representable in binary, fractional shares at an awkward price, a training short, a book underwater); **both** NAV series (`portfolio_nav_daily`'s row and CR136's `portfolio_value_snapshots` total/invested/drawdown) equal `round(oracle, 2)`; TWR across two trading days with a refused open between them reports exactly `0.0` with `capital_event == ["open", None]`; a refused open leaves no leg row, no trade row, no cash movement and no changed valuation — **asserted on the BOOK, not on the refusal**, because the floor already provably says no and the open question was whether saying no is enough; the wire's key set is pinned to the pre-CR172 set plus exactly `options` (`0.1.0+100` is live on TestFlight and Play against this backend); and §3/§11's "`games_scoring_pass` provably untouched" is proven by writing a leg **straight into `sim_option_legs`** against a game portfolio's id, bypassing every check, and finding the portfolio still empty — reaching past the write path deliberately, since asserting the write path refuses would still pass if the READ path folded a leg into a game NAV later. The criterion is not moot: the one thing that can happen is a short call losing the shares that covered it, and that is what `_check_option_margin` is for. **DEF356** proved it reachable two ways — sell the cover out from under a covered call (four ordinary calls; the sale accepted with empty violations, advisories AND not_evaluated), and write two "covered" calls against one lot of 100 shares (each individually covered, the book short 100, no refusal). A pre-trade refusal alone provably cannot close it: `evaluate_outcomes`' bracket close enters no floor at all and correctly so, and there is no user-initiated close path for a structure, so refusing the share sale would trap the user until expiry. **DEF357 is the larger finding: the whole slice-2 lifecycle had no production caller.** `grep -rn "run_option_lifecycle"` returns 21 call sites, every one in its own test file, and zero elsewhere — so on live Alpha an option reached its expiry date and NOTHING happened to it: leg `open` forever, collateral never released, shares never delivered, and the `LifecycleEvent` that exists so *every automatic close is reported, never silent* produced by a function nobody ran. Only criterion 10 (lesson 316-322 amendments + AR/MS flags) remains, alongside the mobile wiring, §11's NAV/FIFO/marks tail and the undecided `risk_budget_usd` split. **CRITERION 10 — ACCEPTANCE COMPLETE, 10 of 10 (2026-08-22, AT:R73).** Swept all seven EN lessons; **three carried the claim, four did not.** 319 ("There's no options trading in AMI Trade — this is a thought exercise"), 320 ("since AMI Trade has no options trading") and 322 ("Remember: AMI Trade has no options trading") were true when written and are not now. 316/317/318/321 never carried it — 321's only near-match is a quiz explanation contrasting a long call's structural floor with a futures obligation, which is instrument arithmetic — and the flag file names them **not stale** explicitly rather than leaving it to inference, because flagging them would cost three translators' time to change nothing. **The amendment states the GATE, it does not flip the claim:** `derivatives_allowed` is False by default, so for almost every reader nothing has changed, and a lesson rewritten to "you can trade options here" would be wrong in the direction that sends someone looking for a button that is not there. 319 now says both structures are simulated *once you turn derivatives on in your mandate* and names the default-off state as deliberate. **320's clause did real work** — it was the reason its not-a-signal warning was true — so deleting it would have left the warning resting on nothing; the warning is rebuilt on its own terms (high implied volatility is a statement about what options COST, and a rich option is not automatically one worth selling). **322 gets the upgrade this CR predicted for it at filing:** the bar the capstone asks the reader to compute is now available PRICED, on a card AMI costed, and watching a simulated OTM call decay to zero on money that was never real is the cheapest version of that lesson there is. F1 — the health check cannot fail:** `main.py:465-467` returns the hardcoded literal `{"status": "ok", "version": "0.1.0", "env": settings.env}`, touching no DB, no Redis, no LLM, no schema revision — and that one endpoint is **both** the container's only healthcheck probe (`docker-compose.yml:400-405`) **and** the promotion's step-7 smoke check, with step 5 *blocking* on `.State.Health.Status == healthy` before calling the deploy successful. it does not add CI). **Acceptance is not "the checks exist" — that is the mistake F1 and F3 already are.** Each new check must be demonstrated **failing against a real broken state before it is trusted**: `/v1/health` still 200 while `/v1/ready` is non-200 against a schema deliberately behind head (both halves recorded); the derived gate set covering `adanos_api_key_secondary` with nobody adding it by hand, and the new test going **red against the pre-fix `_FEATURE_GATES`** before green; `postflight.py` exiting non-zero against a key populated in `infra/alpha.env` and removed from a scratch compose block, naming the missing line; the preflight gate passing today's real 21-line dirty tree and failing on a tracked modification under `backend/`. **NOT claimed on merge:** that promotions become incident-free — this makes the pipeline's own verification honest about what it checked; an honest check that reports a real failure is the deliverable, and a promotion that never fails again is not something a verification layer can promise. **ID note:** filed first as CR173, re-minted to CR175 within the hour — CR173 (Floor v0.2) and CR174 (interactive lesson mode) were both taken by other lanes on the shared checkout while this was being scoped. | CR176 | 2026-08-13 | **Push notifications — the half of CR109's period arc that cannot be built in-app.** CR109 §10.1's matrix marks four beats as *needing* push, and Saiful's ruling was *"in-app ceremony now, push next"*. Slice 5 (Amendment K) built the in-app half; this is the "next". Until it ships, four beats reach only a player who already opened the app — a real hole, because §10 calls the final stretch *"the anticipation engine"* and an anticipation engine nobody is told about is inert. **CORRECTION, 2026-08-13 — this row's original premise was false and is superseded.** It claimed *"No push infrastructure exists at all… no tokens, no APNs, no FCM, no consent flow"*, quoting §10.1, and concluded *"this CR is genuinely infrastructure plus the CR109 beats on top, not a wiring job."* That was already untrue when filed: **CR027 shipped the whole channel** — the OneSignal SDK initialises in `main.dart` before `runApp()`, `users.timezone` exists, `notification_service.notify()` is the single write path with per-user rate limits, a `uq_notifications_dedupe` constraint on `(user_id, type, source_ref)` and CR040-loud `not_configured` handling, `ONESIGNAL_APP_ID`/`ONESIGNAL_REST_KEY` are populated in `infra/alpha.env` and forwarded at `docker-compose.yml:237-238`, and both `price_alert_evaluator` and `daily_reminder` already deliver through it. §10.1's sentence is stale text that this row inherited without checking. **So the delivered scope is a policy layer plus beat queries, not an integration.** **Built:** `games_push.py` — quiet hours evaluated in the user's own `users.timezone`, caps of ≤1/day and ≤4/week counted on the user's LOCAL day, the Close and a received duel challenge exempt from the caps, and a 15-minute `_game_push_tick` in the lifespan. Three of §10.1's four "needed" beats ship: *entries close in 2h and you are not entered* (§10.1's "highest-value push"), *the final stretch*, and *your run has settled*. **One reading of §10.1 rather than a quotation, stated because it is a deviation:** §10.1 says the Close is *"exempt from suppression"*, which read literally fires it at 03:00 local — US settlement lands in the small hours across Asia, and a push that wakes someone is the fastest way to lose the channel the rule exists to protect. Exempt beats therefore bypass the **caps** outright but are **deferred** by quiet hours rather than dropped; the sweep is idempotent on a stable `source_ref`, so the beat sends on the first tick after quiet hours end. It arrives late instead of never. Deferral is safe only because these beats do not expire — the entry beat, which does, carries its own 2-hour window and is simply not eligible outside it, so quiet hours drop it by construction. **Deliberately NOT built: the daily rank-move beat.** §10.1 wants *"You dropped out of the top 10 — once per run"*, which asserts a **change**; `games_board.board_for_run` ranks as of the latest close and takes no as-of date, so a single observation shows where a player is, never that they moved. Firing on "currently outside the top 10" would report a drop that may never have happened — the `?? 0` fabrication shape. Rejected: paging until exhausted on the client (N round trips per tab open, worsening forever) and a backend aggregate endpoint (correct, but the one thing that would stop CR133/CR178 being a pure frontend build). **So every card names its window** — *"your last 100 decisions"* — and that is not a consolation: recency is what a trader can still act on, while an all-time average quietly flattens the month they actually changed how they trade. **Edge cases carried from CR133 §4.1:** `NO_VERDICT` is **not** a rejection (CR098 — folding it into REJECT tells the user their idea was turned down when it was never judged); challenge rows carry `difficulty` so an unweighted comparison must say so; empty-state thresholds rather than degenerate ratios (trades hidden under 3 closes, challenge rows under 5 attempts, drift at one version); bars coloured by **family** (cyan Analysts, amber Risk, purple Research, green Execution), never by member. **Depends on CR133** (`YOU` and its segmented control must exist first). **CR177 would add a sixth candidate card** — *how often AMI stopped you, and which rule* — not claimed here, and CR133 §4.1 measured that a sixth card means one comes out. **Acceptance:** renders no figure it cannot derive and never as `0` (CR040); Measured against the committed 08-13 corpus (482 real production rows): **input context is not a constraint** (largest real prompt **31,544 chars ≈ 6,600–9,000 tokens** against `ami-llm`'s **262,144** — tripling every sheet reaches ~4% of context, **26× headroom**); **cost is not a constraint** (no per-token accounting exists anywhere in `backend/app/`; credits are flat per convene, `credit_service.py:65-97`); **output decode is what breaks, and it is already broken** — truncation is **6/482 = 1.2%** (bull **5%**, bear **5%**, neutral **2.5%**, PM **2.5%**), bull sits at **107% of cap at p95** and neutral at **100%**, and four agents hold only **1.27×–1.56×** headroom at the median. A **+44%** sheet increase historically bought **+14% to +102%** output and took truncation 0/216 → 6/482. **Binding rule:** *any commit that grows a sheet must re-derive `_AGENT_MAX_TOKENS` for bull/bear/neutral/RM/PM in the same commit and carry a post-promotion `finish_reason == "length"` re-measure as its acceptance* — raising the ceiling is free on this host, since `room_prompts.py:167-186` retracted the KV-reservation argument as asserted-not-measured (*"max_tokens is a ceiling, not an allocation"*), while being twenty tokens short costs a stance (CR106) or a whole verdict (DEF258/DEF261). **This CR's own premise was corrected before building, by measurement.** The plan asserted the census is blind to *read-then-dropped* provider keys, citing `totalCash`. A perturbation probe over all 45 regex-consumed keys — change one `.info` value, re-run the real fetcher, see whether any returned value moves — found **zero genuinely inert keys**; `totalCash` *does* influence output (`net_cash`), and the four that showed inert are correct (`pegRatio`/`regularMarketPrice` are fallbacks the all-keys fixture never triggers; `dividendRate`/`exDividendDate` are read in `market_data.py` and reach the profile via `EarningsInfo`). The probe also **caught its own first version being wrong** — an additive perturbation reported `totalDebt`, a demonstrably returned field, as inert, because `round(x / 1_000_000)` swallows a small delta. **So the census needs no rewrite and the real finding is narrower:** perturbing `totalDebt` moves `net_cash` **and** `total_debt`; perturbing `totalCash` moves **only** `net_cash`. Gross debt is rendered, gross cash is not — while `fundamentals.py:271-273` argues explicitly why gross matters beside net (*"$40B cash against $45B debt and $1B against $6B both render as net debt $5,000M, and they are not the same balance sheet"*) and implements only the debt half. Invisible to **both** guards: parity sees only returned keys and `total_cash` is not one; the census sees `totalCash` in source and counts it consumed. Δqueries = **−58,616,264**. | CR197 | 2026-08-19 | **Are the three Risk Debators effective, or two extremes with the answer falling in between?** Saiful's question, answered in two parts. **(1) The suspicion is confirmed for *stances*, refuted for *content*:** across the 118 committed CR143 convenes the Aggressive votes "for" **117/118** and the Conservative "against" **117/118** — role constants carrying ~0 bits about the ticker (only 4 distinct stance triples occur, 3 differing solely in the Neutral); yet role identifiability is 97.5% and the prose cites real per-ticker numbers, so the prompts elicit differentiated *argument* over predetermined *positions*. The Aggressive **structurally cannot debate** — RISK is a single sequential pass (`room_runner.py:151-173`), so it always speaks into a transcript ending at `[trader]` (CR153 F3: 0/18 engagement; upstream runs this as a *cycle*, we flattened it and never rewrote the prompts to match). **(2) "Just use an index for size" contains a false premise — the index already decides size:** the Trader's "proposal" *is* the mandate risk-tier cap, the three debator sizes are computed deterministically *before anyone speaks* (`sizing.py:111-127`, trader+2/−1.5/trader) and handed out to defend, nothing parses a size back out of prose ("never parsed back out of prose", `room_prompts.py:918-921`), and the final size is `min(PM number, risk_tier_cap)`. **Deleting the RISK phase would change zero numeric outputs.** Also found: `parse_stance_envelope` strips the envelope *pre-commit*, so **the PM never sees any debator's stance or conviction** — only prose. What the debate does buy is shipped user-facing product (SSE, Journal replay, 3 of 11 comb voices, 3 unlockable 1-on-1 personas; D-012 locks the roster) at **25% of run cost** (3/12 calls, 24% of decode, 3 serial round-trips). **The causal test has never been run** — CR035 ablated *inputs*, never *stages*; M5 is textual echo, not causation; `kimi/03:282` recommended exactly this and it was never done. Scope: **(A)** offline PM-replay ablation on the committed corpora (V1a/V1b noise floor, V2 debators stripped, V3 extremes stripped) — verified groundwork: audit files carry the verbatim PM prompt, content-join resolves **136/136**, debator turns strip as verbatim blocks **408/408**, production sends **no temperature/top_p** (`max_tokens`=1700), baselines parsed from `response_text` not the floor-vetoed `verdict`; McNemar + Wilson, effects <~8-10pp unresolvable at n=136, contrast internally valid on whatever model serves `ami-llm`. **(B)** additive `SIZE:` field in the debators' stance envelope → `AgentMessage.argued_size_pct`, closing DEF235/CR143 M4 — the metric whose own docstring says *"Zero spread means that phase is costume"* and which has never produced a valid reading. **(C)** surgical prompt rebuild: declare the size, make CONVICTION the honest channel with defined permission to concede, replace the Conservative's double-negative "engage them" (measured ~33% compliance), preserving every string pinned by `test_def241_def243_*`. Out of scope: phase geometry, envelope-in-transcript (would invalidate the Stage A baseline), safety floor. **Delivered 2026-08-19:** `DEBATE_SIGNAL.md` + `REPORT.md`; `scripts/debate_signal_report.py` (deterministic, no LLM); `scripts/pm_debate_ablation.py` **dry-run green — 136/136 joins, 408/408 strips, zero network**; SIZE envelope field → `AgentMessage.argued_size_pct` through `agent_done` + journal freeze; the three `.md` rebuilds + overlay conviction bullets; M4 rewritten to read the field, report `declaration_rate`, and state that the handed spread is 3.5 pt by construction; `test_cr197_size_envelope.py` (31 tests) and a CR158 fix — its guard had gone **vacuous** for debators the moment the envelope contract split, so it now pins both constants. Suite **4459 passed / 3 skipped**. **ABLATION RUN 2026-08-20 — 816 calls, 6 arms, 0 errors, against `ami-llm` = Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 (the model that produced the corpora).** Result, and it splits Saiful's question in two: **the debate as a stage is causally load-bearing** — strip all three debators and approvals halve, 22→10 (16.3%→7.4%), APPROVE→PASS 14 vs PASS→APPROVE 2, exact McNemar **p=0.004**, spread over **9 tickers and 3 epochs** — while **the two extremes are inert to the decision**: strip both and nothing moves (17.2% vs 16.3% baseline, net **−1**, p=1.0, the tightest null in the set). Every arm keeping the Neutral sits at baseline (15.7–17.2%); every arm without it falls (7.4–11.9%), and surviving-debator COUNT does not order the table (v3 keeps one and scores highest, v4 keeps two and scores low). **Two methodological saves, both of which changed the answer.** (1) The pre-registered statistic was the wrong instrument — it compared SYMMETRIC flip rates and returned p=1.0 "not demonstrated", because noise flips balance (8 up / 8 down) while ablation flips do not (14 down / 2 up), so the APPROVE count halves with the flip rate unmoved; marginal homogeneity was the hypothesis all along. (2) The deflationary explanation was tested rather than assumed — approval rate initially tracked WHO SPOKE LAST, ordered by that voice's negativity (Neutral 15.7–17.2% > Conservative 11.9% > Trader 7.4%), which pure recency anchoring explains without the debate carrying information; **arm v5 refutes it** by leaving the always-bullish Aggressive (117/118 "for") speaking last while deleting two thirds of the debate — anchoring predicts ≥baseline, observed **10.3%, second-lowest**. **Mechanism identified: option generation, not persuasion.** The debate hands the PM a middle-sized alternative it does not construct alone (AVGO: with debate → APPROVE down-sized 3.0%→1.5% citing the Conservative's stop; without → PASS on 1:1 risk/reward); without it 8 of 10 approvals sit at exactly the Trader's 3.0%. **The trap, stated explicitly: v3 does NOT license deleting the extremes** — every arm holds surviving turns fixed at what was recorded, and the Neutral's turn was written in a room where the extremes spoke; its job is to synthesise them. Two readings the data cannot separate (correcting DEF066's ~20× overstatement vs. DEF292's "budget is effectively empty" from the other side), so it **ships gated OFF** behind `PM_OPTION_LADDER_ENABLED` with both readings recorded in the setting's own docstring — a ~5pp swing in approval rate is a product call, not an implementation detail. **(2) CIO self-consistency** (`_vote_pm_samples` + `PM_SELF_CONSISTENCY_SAMPLES`, default 1 = today's single call): majority on action, **median** size among winners so narration matches the numbers that ship, ties → PASS per DEF059. Same class as DEF335 and DEF379: an artifact whose confident surface stops the next reader looking. **A CR and not a DEF** — the spec asked for `level_provenance`-gated target/stop-hit and delivered it; what the acceptance criteria never asked was what the counts should be compared to. **Scope:** print, beside the existing counts, (1) level geometry over the stated levels of all scoreable runs — mean/median stop and target distance as % of entry and the resulting R:R — computed from `room_runs` and **not** from realized exits, since the hit-only subsample is biased toward close levels on both legs and correcting that bias is the main reason this belongs in code; (2) the driftless-RW first-touch null `target/(stop+target)` on both mean and median geometry, beside the observed stop-first share with its z; (3) a label making the null a null — what the counts look like under no skill, not a target and not a threshold. **Constraints:** `level_provenance` gating unchanged (`ami_default` stays excluded — a minted `entry*0.94`/`entry*1.13` pair would hard-code a 2.17 : 1 R:R and make the statistic meaningless); **never a promotion gate**, same rule `RETEST_RECIPE.md` binds the edge number to, and at 22 first-touches it has no power to gate anything; byte-reproducibility preserved (no new RNG, no unsorted iteration); and the report must name the window mismatch — target/stop-hit spans a fixed 20 trading days while the P&L table walks each trade to its own stated horizon (median 90 days), which is part of why the two were never read against each other. **Acceptance:** unit tests on the geometry and null (a provenance-excluded leg contributes to neither; a symmetric 1 : 1 R:R yields a 50% null; a fixture lopsided purely by geometry produces a null matching the observed share); `pytest backend/tests/unit/ -q` green; report re-run byte-identical on unchanged DB state; and the pinned-batch baseline table in `CR164_room_backtest/RETEST_RECIPE.md` re-diffed against a re-run, since this changes `report_*.md` bytes — the ~1.5 h routine the recipe exists for, and the main cost here. **Priority: low** — it prevents a repeat of a misreading that has happened once and is now corrected in the document a future reader reaches first; it should not go ahead of DEF335's `auto_adjust=False` re-backfill (119,311 rows, 201 tickers). Out of scope: any change to how the Room sets levels (nothing established a defect there — the correction found the opposite), and re-running `r70-outcome-2` (its numbers are unchanged). | CR221 | 2026-09-03 | **The Room named 49 distinct data items it lacks; 36 are open, and 35 of those have a verified FREE source — none needs a paid provider.** CR219 put a `DATA I LACKED:` addendum on every turn of six mandate arms plus one full live convene: **127 request lines from 12 agents**. 127 is how *loud* the demand is, not how much data is missing — one ticker through seven convenes repeats heavily (the maturity ladder alone is 14 lines from 6 agents), so this CR deduplicates to **49 items at one-item-per-distinct-ask**, checks each against the six fields CR219 shipped, and finds each remainder a source. **9 delivered** (A5 interest coverage, B5 own-history multiples, C1 capex, C6 buyback pacing, E1/E2 revisions+surprise, F10 ATR, J1 raw social split, K1 Decision Journal), **4 closed** (guidance ruled out by R22; Level 2 depth and dark-pool prints have no free source; sentiment history is structurally absent — the cache keeps one row by design), **36 open**. Bonfield, who retires 2026-10-01, which is precisely what the News Analyst asked in 5 of 7 convenes and once tagged `ABSENT`, out of a filing we already download; **FRED's `fredgraph.csv` needs no API key** and serves H1/H3 (`CPIAUCSL` 332.813, `PPIACO` 284.057, `TTLCONS` 2,157,581, `HOUST` 1,239, all through 2026-07-01) — ISM's PMI is proprietary and 404s, so the free substitutes `CFNAI`/`IPMAN`/`DGORDER` must be named honestly rather than labelled "PMI"; yfinance `growth_estimates`/`eps_trend` serve C9/E4 (`LTG` is NaN for CAT → absent state); the free keyless US Treasury par-yield CSV is available as a derivation input. The data is real at a different endpoint: CAT's 10-K `0000018230-26-000008` indexes `R106.htm` (long-term debt by *Machinery, Power & Energy* vs. Financial Products), `R108.htm` (the ladder), `R129.htm` (disaggregation of revenue) and `R136.htm` (geographic areas) via `FilingSummary.xml` — 30 request lines across A2/A4/D1/D2 ride that one route. Reported to the WP10 lane with its repro; its files untouched. **R38 RULED 2026-09-03 (`ac55352c`): declared-absent entry in CR219 now, re-route under CR221 later** — WP10's escape hatch fired on the same evidence independently, and its full build (5 source files, 83 green tests) is parked at `CR219/dev_instructions/WP10_R38_parked/` as this CR's head start; only the route changes. **§7 adds the measurement Saiful required: once built, re-run CR219's own convenes with the new data and conclude how much difference it makes.** The primary endpoint is deliberately NOT the verdict — `risk_officer.py:32` records 19.7% of convenes splitting across byte-identical inputs, so a verdict that moves after a field lands is indistinguishable from a coin at any affordable n. Secondary endpoints: citation rate per new line (the precedent is margin structure 95.5% vs margin trend 24.2% on identical sheets), reasoning-trace presence, and the cost delta. Every shipped item ends at zero asks in its own arm — A1 1→0, C3 3→1→0, C4 0→1→0 — and **none of it is attributable**, because the negative control fell harder than any treatment: D1+A2, with nothing built for either and both predicted flat, go **17 → 6 → 6**, a 65% fall. The totals are the mechanism: **54 / 56 / 50**, flat, while individual items swing by 7 — the `DATA I LACKED` addendum is a **rank-limited shortlist, not a census**, so filling one gap promotes the next into the slot and per-item differences measure re-ranking, not satisfaction.
